description: Machine-readable selection, composition, delivery, ownership, and accessibility metadata for Kerf UI, plus the optional Web Awesome integration set.

entries.name: Badge
entries.description: Self-styled, non-interactive status, count, and category metadata configured through semantic tone, appearance, shape, and size props.
entries.purpose: Present compact metadata without application-authored badge CSS or consumer styling of component internals.
useWhen: Show a short status, count, category, or metadata label whose presentation should be configured rather than restyled.
avoidWhen: Do not use Badge as a button, link, or removable chip; choose an interactive control with the correct native semantics.
Do not rely on tone alone to communicate meaning.
variants: neutral, info, pop, success, warning, or danger tone
compact or default size, or a text-free dot (size: 'dot')
maxWidth caps the badge and truncates long text with an ellipsis, defaulting the title to string or number content
accessibility: Badge is non-interactive. Supply label when visible content is abbreviated, and ariaHidden when it repeats an accessible name owned by the surrounding component. A text-free dot must take either label (exposed as an image) or ariaHidden, which the types enforce.
Keep meaningful text visible because tone is supplementary.
A label replaces abbreviated or symbolic visible text; the badge is then a labeled image (role img).

entries.name: Chip
entries.description: A short tag with semantic or inherited tone, an optional accessible remove button, a native link and download form, or a native action button, including compact and disabled variants.
entries.purpose: Render removable tags, file or link chips, and activatable action chips without application rules on Web Awesome internals or anchor and button chrome.
useWhen: Show a short tag that the application can remove through a delegated action, including a compact or disabled tag.
Show a downloadable file or a short link with chip geometry, such as the referenced files of a chat message; set tone inherit inside a brand-loud or neutral ContentItem bubble.

Offer a short value the user can activate to apply it, such as a filter token in a search syntax help popover that inserts itself into the query: set action (and itemId) so the whole chip is a native button.
avoidWhen: Use Badge for non-interactive status and count metadata.
Do not use the remove button without a specific accessible name.
Use ListItemLink for a navigation row and ToolbarActionLink for a toolbar link.
Use ChoiceChips when the chips choose a persistent value with radio or checkbox state; an action chip fires a one-shot command.
appOwns: link destination and download file name
variants: neutral, info, pop, success, warning, danger, or inherit tone
removable, link, action, or plain, enabled or disabled
accessibility: The remove control is a native button and requires an action and a specific removeLabel. A disabled chip disables that button and removes it from keyboard interaction.

A link chip is a native anchor named by its visible label; external adds a safe rel, a new tab, and an "(opens in new tab)" name suffix, and a disabled link chip drops its destination and leaves the tab order.
The inherit tone paints no fill, so its label keeps the surrounding text contrast, and its focus ring follows the surrounding foreground.

An action chip is one native button (type button) named by its visible label or by actionLabel, which should include that label; Enter and Space activate it, it shows the focus ring on keyboard focus, and a disabled action chip is a disabled button that leaves the tab order. It cannot also be a link or carry a remove button.
Keep meaningful tag text visible because tone is supplementary.

entries.name: LucideIcon
entries.description: Decorative and meaningfully labeled Lucide-compatible icons.
entries.purpose: Decorative and meaningfully labeled Lucide-compatible icons.
useWhen: Render a decorative or explicitly labeled Lucide-compatible icon in Kerf application UI.
avoidWhen: Do not use an icon as the only name of an unfamiliar action.
variants: hover title for a status icon

usageExamples.title: Solid selected glyph
usageExamples.description: The solid appearance fills a compatible Lucide glyph with currentColor while retaining its stroke and accessible name policy.

usageExamples.title: Semantic icon color
usageExamples.description: Set an icon foreground with a semantic color token; omit color to inherit from surrounding text. Use foregroundColor() for a custom CSS color or foregroundColorVar() for an app variable.

usageExamples.title: Inline with text
usageExamples.description: Let a decorative icon flow inside Text or other prose while preserving its inherited 1em size.

accessibility: Decorative icons are aria-hidden; meaningful icons require a label.
title adds an SVG <title> as hover text over the whole icon box (a transparent hit box fills the 24-unit view box); with label, the label stays the name, and alone the title names the icon.

entries.name: DisclosureArrow
entries.description: Root-scaled 18px animated open and closed disclosure indicator with configurable directions, shortest-path rotation, and right-oriented replacement icon content.
entries.purpose: Indicate whether a disclosure control is open with an overridable 18px root-scaled visual and shortest-path rotation behavior.
useWhen: Add a shortest-path rotating indicator to a control that owns open and closed state; author replacement icon content facing right before direction transforms are applied.
avoidWhen: Do not use the arrow as the interactive control or accessible name by itself.
accessibility: The arrow is decorative; expose expanded state through aria-expanded on its owning control and keep that control's accessible name stable.

entries.name: Foundation Tokens
entries.description: The complete public typography, spacing, breakpoint, geometry, radius, color, focus, and shadow token surface shipped by foundation.css.
entries.purpose: Provide the shared semantic token foundation for application themes and every styled Kerf UI component.
useWhen: Theme a Kerf application globally or reuse the shipped semantic typography, spacing, geometry, color, focus, and shadow values in application-owned composition CSS.
avoidWhen: Do not replace a component-specific prop or token with a broad foundation override when only one component instance should change.
appOwns: responsive policy at the cataloged device-class breakpoints
accessibility: Preserve semantic contrast relationships and the visible focus ring when overriding foundation colors.

entries.name: Document Baseline
entries.description: Opt-in document-level defaults: border-box sizing, body margin/font/surface, native table-cell and form-control font metrics, semantic control cursors, link color, and the html → body → .kui-app-root full-height chain.
entries.purpose: Let an application opt into Kerf UI-owned document defaults and a definite full-height chain for a percentage-height application shell.
useWhen: An application wants Kerf UI to own document-level box sizing, body typography, native table-cell and form-control font metrics, surface, and link color.
A full-height shell (Workbench, SplitView, NavStack, or TabNavigator) mounts into one direct container: put .kui-app-root on that container.
avoidWhen: Do not put .kui-app-root on several sibling containers; each requests the full available document height.
Do not import it where the host page already owns document-level defaults it would override.

alternatives.when: Import the foundation tokens the baseline reads; the baseline itself adds only global document selectors.

appOwns: application overrides loaded after the baseline
variants: viewport-locked application root (data-viewport="locked" on a body-child .kui-app-root: 100dvh and overflow clip on html, body, and the root)
accessibility: Links keep the semantic link color at zero specificity so application focus and link styles still apply.

Native controls get semantic cursors at zero specificity: pointer on enabled buttons, links, role=button, checkbox/radio/button-type inputs, selects, and checkbox/radio labels; not-allowed on disabled controls, aria-disabled role=button, and a disabled wa-button's base part; text on text-like inputs and textareas.

notes: The body margin is removed; .kui-app-root only sets height: 100% and owns no inset.

entries.name: Application Layout
entries.description: Unpadded panes, 24px content stacks, and self-contained 8/1/8 content items for application layout boundaries.
entries.purpose: Provide one reusable pane, toolbar, content stack, and content-item geometry across sidebars, main areas, and dialogs.
useWhen: Build sidebars, main areas, inspectors, or dialogs from an unpadded pane with optional toolbar/footer and one content stack.
Relocate a hidden pane's restore control into the adjacent main toolbar on the same logical edge.
avoidWhen: Do not pad the pane itself or add wrapper insets around children that already own content-item geometry.
Do not leave an empty icon-only rail after collapsing a pane.
appOwns: pane visibility and matching collapse/restore controls
variants: hidden inline-start pane restored from main-toolbar leading
hidden inline-end pane restored from main-toolbar trailing
accessibility: Keep reading and focus order coherent when controls wrap or panes relocate, and preserve one scroll owner per pane.
When collapse replaces one control with its counterpart in another toolbar, move focus to the newly rendered restore or collapse control.

entries.name: Pane
entries.description: An unpadded application column with optional vertical header/footer slots, one scrolling vertical content stack, and independent logical-edge separators.
entries.purpose: Organize a sidebar, main area, inspector, or dialog column into fixed vertical header/footer chrome around one scrolling content owner.
useWhen: An application column needs shared header, content, and optional footer organization with exactly one scrolling content owner.
A pane boundary needs an opt-in separator on any combination of logical sides.
Pinned chrome needs a divider from the scrolling content only while content is scrolled beneath it (wireScrollDividers).
A lowered background must cover the scrolling work viewport and blank space after short content without a second scroll container (appearance: sunken).
A child table or other component needs edge-to-edge decoration with text aligned to other pane content.
An opaque edge-to-edge child needs a reserved vertical scrollbar gutter.
Scrolling content must pass beneath chrome laid over the pane edge (a DialogSurface floating footer) while its first and last items still rest clear of it (scrollClearance).

The header should float over the scrolling content on a translucent material so content scrolls visibly beneath it, with the first item still resting below the header (headerPresentation: overlay, measured by wireScrollDividers).
A pane needs an app-chosen surface color, such as a media detail page painted in its artwork's color (background, a typed CssColor; also in PaneConfig).

A region should take on an app color (a media page in its artwork's color) with its text, quiet text, links, fills, and chrome material re-derived to keep AA (tint: { color, scheme }; also in PaneConfig).

The header lies over imagery and must be fully transparent, with glass control groups for legibility and the material fading back in once content scrolls beneath (headerPresentation: clear, scrollEdge: material).
avoidWhen: Do not use Pane as a padded card or add a competing scroll owner around its content slot.
Do not enable separators merely as decoration; use them only where the pane owns a real boundary.

A ToolbarText description in an overlay header is fine: an untoned ToolbarText there takes the normal text color for its title and lifts its description halfway toward it, keeping AA over the content passing beneath. Do not put other quiet secondary text in an overlay header; keep it in the content.

alternatives.when: Use the layout content-item and control classes inside Pane when children need shared geometry.

appOwns: which sides may compensate for device safe areas in an app-owned arrangement (safeAreaEdges)
whether the chrome dividers follow the scroll, always show, or never show (chromeDividers)
default or sunken scrolling work surface (appearance)
whether to reserve a vertical scrollbar gutter for opaque edge-to-edge content (--kui-pane-scrollbar-gutter)
optional keyboard or programmatic focus (tabIndex) and persistent focus outline (outlined)

whether the scrolling content clears overlaying chrome on its block edges (scrollClearance, also in PaneConfig, so a Workbench mainPane or panel pane, a CollapsiblePanel pane, or a NavStack view pane forwards it)
whether the header is docked in its own row or laid over the scrolling content on the translucent chrome material (headerPresentation, also in PaneConfig)

an optional app-chosen surface color that replaces the appearance's fill (background, a typed CssColor from @kerfjs/ui/css-values, also in PaneConfig, so a Workbench panel or mainPane, a CollapsiblePanel pane, or a NavStack view pane forwards it)
an optional scoped tint (tint: { color, scheme }, also in PaneConfig): the color and the declared light or dark scheme it belongs to; Kerf does no color detection
an optional tint accent (tint.accent) that re-derives the brand ramp, links, and focus ring inside the tinted scope at AA
variants: chrome dividers only while scrolled (default, wired by wireScrollDividers)
scrollClearance block-start, block-end, or both on the scrolling content
overlay header on the translucent chrome material (headerPresentation: overlay)
app-chosen background color (background), replacing the default or sunken fill
scoped tint re-deriving surface and text tokens from an app color (tint)
clear (transparent) overlay header, optionally with the scroll-edge material (headerPresentation: clear, scrollEdge: material)
accessibility: Choose semantic root and content elements that match the region and provide labels for landmark elements.
Keep fixed header/footer chrome outside the single scrolling content slot so reading and focus order remain coherent.

An overlay header's text uses the normal text color, which keeps WCAG AA over the 80% chrome material on any content; the material turns opaque under prefers-reduced-transparency, prefers-contrast: more, forced colors, or without backdrop-filter.
A background color is app-chosen: Keep text at WCAG AA over the color: a dark background needs dark-tone content or a scoped tint; forced colors paint Canvas instead.

A tint clamps the re-derived surface and text lightness so normal, quiet, link, and neutral-on-quiet text keep 4.5:1 over the tinted surface, raised surface, and quiet fills for any color; under prefers-contrast: more or without relative color syntax the scope keeps the plain palette in its declared scheme.

A clear header has no material of its own: keep its controls in glass ToolbarControlGroups and a title over imagery on a scrim; it turns opaque under reduced transparency or increased contrast and paints Canvas in forced colors.

notes: The pane is unpadded; separators are independently opt-in on logical edges and default off.

Safe areas: the root and separators paint through unsafe areas while header, content, and footer pad the sides the pane still reaches (routed by --kui-edge-inset-*); content block insets are scroll padding.
The scrolling content exposes its resolved logical inline padding to descendants as --kui-pane-content-inset-inline-start/end, including safe areas and deepInset.
deepInset adds --kui-space-xs to every side of the scrolling content and its block scroll padding; header/footer chrome still owns safe-area padding at its edge.
For opaque edge-to-edge children, --kui-pane-scrollbar-gutter: stable reserves a vertical scrollbar gutter outside the published content insets; the default is auto.

scrollClearance adds the inherited --kui-scroll-clearance-block-start/end context, published by overlaying chrome, to the scrolling content block padding and scroll padding alongside safe areas and deepInset.

headerPresentation overlay: once wireScrollDividers measures the header, the header shares the content cell above the scroller, its border-box height is published as --kui-scroll-clearance-block-start on the Pane root, and the content clears it automatically; unwired or with chromePlacement auto, the header stays docked.

The scrolling content also publishes its resolved block-start padding (safe area, deepInset, and overlay or clear header clearance) as --kui-pane-content-inset-block-start, so a first child such as an underChrome BackdropImage can run up beneath it.

stateAttributes.name: data-scroll-overflow
stateAttributes.meaning: The physical edges, in canonical t/r/b/l order, beyond which content is scrolled out of view; absent when nothing is hidden (content that fits never reports its far edges). Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

stateAttributes.name: data-scroll-divider
stateAttributes.meaning: The sides, in t/r/b/l order, on which this chrome currently draws its scroll divider: the side facing the scroller while content is hidden beyond it. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

stateAttributes.name: data-header-overlay
stateAttributes.meaning: measured once the wiring has measured an overlay header (headerPresentation: overlay) and published its border-box height as --kui-scroll-clearance-block-start on the Pane root (and a classic content scrollbar's inline size as --kui-pane-scrollbar-inline-size, which the header leaves uncovered); the header then lies over the content, which clears it. Both are re-applied if a re-render drops them.

entries.name: NavStack
entries.description: A controlled one-pane navigation stack that keeps prior views mounted, slides content on push and pop, cross-fades per-view chrome, and moves/restores focus.
entries.purpose: Present a single linear or drill-down flow while preserving each prior view's state, scroll position, and place in the stack.
useWhen: A compact surface shows one view at a time and navigation pushes into details or pops back.
A simple single-pane screen needs the same stable app-layout contract without any nested navigation.
avoidWhen: Do not use NavStack when a list and detail should remain visible together; use SplitView.
Do not use it for co-equal top-level destinations on compact devices; wrap one stack per destination in TabNavigator.

alternatives.when: Promote a list-to-detail stack to SplitView once both regions fit together.
Use one NavStack as each TabNavigator tab's persistent content.
Use ContentSwap to swap content in place inside one region without navigation chrome.

appOwns: ordered view stack and stable keys
view content and structured top and bottom toolbar configurations
preferred initial focus targets when DOM order is insufficient
per-view bottom toolbar or a persistent structured fallback
per-view leading, center, and trailing top-toolbar groups
per-view header and footer with List and Pane configuration
top-toolbar defaults, title size, and heading level
whether the chrome and bottom-toolbar dividers follow the scroll, always show, or never show (chromeDividers)
whether the top chrome docks above the active view or lies over it on the translucent chrome material (chromePresentation)
whether the bottom toolbar docks below the active view or lies over it on the translucent chrome material (bottomToolbarPresentation)
an optional app-chosen color for the stack, its docked chrome and bottom toolbar, and every view (background, a typed CssColor); one view's own color goes in its pane: { background }
an optional scoped tint for the stack, its chrome, and views: tint: { color, scheme } re-derives surface and text tokens from an app color with text kept at AA
variants: custom back icon or visible back text
persistent final top-toolbar group (panelToggle) when embedded in a Workbench panel
chrome and bottom-toolbar dividers only while the active view scrolls beneath them (wired by wireScrollDividers)
permanent or no chrome dividers (chromeDividers always or none)
translucent top chrome laid over the active view (chromePresentation overlay, measured by wireNavStack)
translucent bottom toolbar laid over the active view (bottomToolbarPresentation overlay, measured by wireNavStack)
app-chosen stack background color (background); overlay chrome keeps the chrome material
clear (transparent) bars with an optional scroll-edge material (chromePresentation / bottomToolbarPresentation: clear, scrollEdge: material)
accessibility: Give the stack region an accessible label and every back control a stable action label; visible backText names the control itself.
Set toolbarConfig.headingLevel when the view title is the page's or section's heading landmark.
Use wireNavStack so each controlled push moves focus into the new top view and each pop restores the revealed view's remembered descendant.
Mark a preferred initial heading or control with data-nav-focus when the first enabled focusable descendant is not the right target.

Overlay chrome (chromePresentation overlay) keeps WCAG AA over content passing beneath the translucent material: an untoned ToolbarText there takes the normal text color for its title and lifts its description halfway toward it; keep other quiet copy in the view. The material turns opaque under reduced transparency, increased contrast, forced colors, or without backdrop-filter.

An overlay bottom toolbar (bottomToolbarPresentation overlay) keeps the same AA rule: an untoned ToolbarText there lifts its title and description, and a default-tone ToolbarControlGroup in either overlaid bar takes the normal text color for its controls. Its 1px top edge stays visible in forced colors.
A background color is app-chosen: Keep text at WCAG AA over the color: a dark background needs dark-tone content or a scoped tint; forced colors paint Canvas instead.
Clear bars have no material of their own: keep their controls in glass ToolbarControlGroups; they turn opaque under reduced transparency or increased contrast and paint Canvas in forced colors.

notes: The stack owns its full-height chrome and viewport; each view owns its internal content padding and scrollable content.

The top chrome's bottom line and the bottom toolbar's top line are scroll state (wireScrollDividers), drawn as an overlaid 1px pseudo-element on the chrome and the bottom toolbar's always-present 1px top border, so neither moves the chrome or the content.

chromePresentation overlay: once wireNavStack measures the live chrome (never a cross-fading copy), the chrome lies over the viewport's top edge and its border-box height, top safe area included, becomes the viewport's block-start --kui-edge-inset-* context, so a plain view, a sole Pane, or a nested layout pads and scroll-pads by it automatically; the chrome ends where a classic scrollbar in the active view begins, so its track stays uncovered; unwired, or with hideToolbar, the chrome stays docked.

bottomToolbarPresentation overlay: once wireNavStack measures the live bottom toolbar (never a cross-fading copy), the toolbar lies over the viewport's bottom edge and its border-box height, bottom safe area and divider border included, becomes the viewport's block-end --kui-edge-inset-* context, so a plain view, a sole Pane (its content, or its footer), or a nested layout pads and scroll-pads by it automatically and the last item rests just above the toolbar; it ends where a classic scrollbar in the active view begins; unwired, or while no bottom toolbar is shown, it stays docked. It is independent of chromePresentation, which governs only the top chrome.

stateAttributes.name: data-nav-chrome-transition
stateAttributes.meaning: "true" while the chrome cross-fades between the outgoing and incoming view.

stateAttributes.name: data-nav-chrome-copy
stateAttributes.meaning: Marks the inert, aria-hidden snapshot of the outgoing chrome shown during the cross-fade.

stateAttributes.name: data-nav-revealed
stateAttributes.meaning: "true" on the preserved, aria-hidden previous view while an incoming view slides over it.

stateAttributes.name: data-nav-exiting
stateAttributes.meaning: "true" on a popped view the helper briefly re-inserts to slide it out.

Both are re-applied if a re-render drops them.

stateAttributes.name: data-bottom-toolbar-overlay
stateAttributes.meaning: measured once the helper has measured an overlay bottom toolbar (bottomToolbarPresentation: overlay) and published its border-box height on the stack root; the toolbar then lies over the active view, which clears it through the block-end edge context. Both are re-applied if a re-render drops them.

stateAttributes.name: data-scroll-overflow
stateAttributes.on: the active kui-nav-stack__view, or the kui-pane__content of a sole Pane in it
stateAttributes.meaning: The physical edges, in canonical t/r/b/l order, beyond which content is scrolled out of view; absent when nothing is hidden (content that fits never reports its far edges). Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

stateAttributes.name: data-scroll-divider
stateAttributes.meaning: The sides, in t/r/b/l order, on which this chrome currently draws its scroll divider: the side facing the scroller while content is hidden beyond it. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

stateAttributes.name: data-header-overlay
stateAttributes.meaning: measured once the wiring has measured a Pane's overlay header (headerPresentation: overlay) and published its border-box height as --kui-scroll-clearance-block-start on the Pane root, plus a classic content scrollbar's inline size as --kui-pane-scrollbar-inline-size, which the header leaves uncovered. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

entries.name: SplitView
entries.description: A responsive list-detail layout that shows both panes on roomy device classes and collapses to a navigation stack on compact classes.
entries.purpose: Present a selectable list and its detail together when space permits, with a one-pane drill-down replacement on compact devices.
useWhen: Selection in a primary list updates a related detail pane and both should remain visible on roomy device classes.
The same list-detail flow must become a navigation stack on a handset or portrait tablet.
avoidWhen: Do not use SplitView for a single linear flow; use NavStack.
Do not use it for a complex desktop tool with multiple peripheral panels; use Workbench.

alternatives.when: SplitView renders the one-pane navigation-stack form on compact device classes.
Use Workbench when a desktop-class tool needs more than the list and detail regions.

appOwns: optional list collapse state and its restore control
compact list and detail toolbar groups, toolbar configuration, and chrome dividers
variants: fixed roomy split with listWidth: a pixel size, optionally capped at a fraction of the split's width
collapsed resizable list with a restore control
accessibility: Give the overall split and both meaningful panes accessible labels.
Wire the compact back action and optional separator keyboard behavior, and restore focus when controlled navigation replaces a view.

notes: The root owns the two-column split and the list pane owns its separator; list and detail content own their internal padding and scroll behavior.

stateAttributes.name: data-handle-inset
stateAttributes.meaning: Present while a clipping edge clamps the region: the handle and its focus ring sit inside the region instead of overhanging that edge.

stateAttributes.name: data-resizing
stateAttributes.meaning: "true" during an active pointer drag of the handle.

stateAttributes.name: data-nav-chrome-transition
stateAttributes.meaning: "true" while the chrome cross-fades between the outgoing and incoming view.

stateAttributes.name: data-nav-chrome-copy
stateAttributes.meaning: Marks the inert, aria-hidden snapshot of the outgoing chrome shown during the cross-fade.

stateAttributes.name: data-nav-revealed
stateAttributes.meaning: "true" on the preserved, aria-hidden previous view while an incoming view slides over it.

stateAttributes.name: data-nav-exiting
stateAttributes.meaning: "true" on a popped view the helper briefly re-inserts to slide it out.

stateAttributes.name: data-chrome-overlay
stateAttributes.meaning: measured once the helper has measured the compact stack's overlay chrome (compactStack.chromePresentation: overlay) and published its border-box height on the stack root. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

stateAttributes.name: data-bottom-toolbar-overlay
stateAttributes.meaning: measured once the helper has measured the compact stack's overlay bottom toolbar (compactStack.bottomToolbarPresentation: overlay) and published its border-box height on the stack root. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

entries.name: TabNavigator
entries.description: A controlled compact-device bottom tab navigator that keeps every destination scene mounted so its navigation and scroll state survive selection changes.
entries.purpose: Switch among two to five co-equal top-level destinations on compact devices while preserving each destination's independent content state.
useWhen: A handset or portrait-tablet app has two to five co-equal top-level destinations.
Each destination must stay mounted so its NavStack and scroll position survive tab switches.
avoidWhen: Do not use TabNavigator for document tabs or reorderable work items; use TabBar.
Do not retain the bottom bar on desktop when the same destinations should be promoted to a Workbench rail or sidebar.

alternatives.when: Use TabBar and TabBarItem for document-style tabpanels, overflow, closing, or reordering.
Promote top-level destinations to a rail or sidebar on desktop-class layouts.

appOwns: tab badge counts or dots and their localized badgeLabel phrases
responsive replacement on larger device classes
whether the bar divider follows the scroll, always shows, or never shows (chromeDividers)
whether the bar's top separator follows a sunken active surface or stays hidden (separator)
optional active-scene focus (tabIndex) and persistent outline (outlined)
an optional app-chosen color for the navigator and its docked bar (background) and per scene (tab.background), each a typed CssColor that replaces the default or sunken fill
an optional scoped tint for the navigator (tint) or one scene (tab.tint): tint: { color, scheme } re-derives surface and text tokens from an app color with text kept at AA
variants: bar divider only while the active scene continues below it (wired by wireScrollDividers)
permanent or no bar divider (chromeDividers always or none)
sunken active-scene separator (separator auto or hidden)
translucent tab bar laid over the active scene (barPresentation overlay, measured by wireTabNavigator)

clear (transparent) bars with an optional scroll-edge material (barPresentation: clear, scrollEdge: material)
accessibility: Give the tablist an accessible label and keep exactly the active tab in the sequential focus order.
Wire selection through the controlled active id while leaving inactive scenes mounted and hidden.
A focusable scene is a tabpanel named by its tab label; optional scene tabIndex applies only while active.

A tab badge is aria-hidden; supply badgeLabel so the tab's accessible name becomes "<label>, <badgeLabel>" (it defaults to the badge text). The dot form, badge: true, has no text, so its badgeLabel is required.

Over the overlay bar's translucent material, unselected labels lift halfway toward --kui-color-text and the selected label mixes 40% of it into the brand color, so both keep 4.5:1 over worst-case content; the material turns opaque under reduced transparency or increased contrast and paints Canvas with a CanvasText edge in forced colors.
A background color is app-chosen: Keep text at WCAG AA over the color: a dark background needs dark-tone content or a scoped tint; forced colors paint Canvas instead.
Clear bars have no material of their own: keep their controls in glass ToolbarControlGroups; they turn opaque under reduced transparency or increased contrast and paint Canvas in forced colors.

notes: The navigator owns the full-height scene region and safe-area-aware bottom bar; scene content owns its internal geometry.
The bar's reserved 1px top edge separates a sunken active scene or nested Pane by default; on flat surfaces it follows scroll state (wireScrollDividers). separator=hidden suppresses it.

barPresentation=overlay: once wireTabNavigator has measured the live bar (data-bar-overlay=measured), the bar is absolutely positioned over the scenes on --kui-chrome-material and the scenes route its border-box height (bottom safe area included) as the block-end --kui-edge-inset-* context, so a plain scene pads and scroll-pads by it and a sole Pane or NavStack clears it; unwired it stays docked.

stateAttributes.meaning: The physical edges, in canonical t/r/b/l order, beyond which content is scrolled out of view; absent when nothing is hidden (content that fits never reports its far edges). Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

entries.name: Workbench
entries.description: A desktop-class multi-panel workspace with independently collapsible, optionally drag-resizable left and right rails and a bottom drawer around one central work area.
entries.purpose: Arrange a complex tool or editor as a stable central work area with optional peripheral rails and a bottom drawer.
useWhen: A desktop-class tool needs a central work area plus independently collapsible navigator, inspector, or console regions.
A desktop-class tool should let people size its peripheral panels by dragging or with the keyboard; opt each panel in with resizable and wire it with wireWorkbench.
avoidWhen: Do not shrink the full multi-panel shell onto compact devices; present peripheral content through NavStack or overlay drawers instead.
Do not use Workbench for one standalone collapsible rail or drawer; use CollapsiblePanel.
Do not offer resizing where rails present as compact overlay drawers or are replaced; set a panel's responsiveOverlayAt, or pass deviceClass so wireWorkbench suspends resizing on compact classes.

alternatives.when: Use Pane inside Workbench regions when fixed header/footer chrome must surround one scroll owner.

appOwns: optional accessible name for the central region (mainLabel)
navigation panel view stack and push/pop actions when navStack is supplied
optional main and panel focus stops and persistent outlines
variants: navigation panel with per-screen toolbar, fixed header, and one scroll owner; standard toggle remains last and relocates while collapsed
opt-in drag and keyboard resizable panels with min/max limits
resizable rails that leave the work area a minimum width and shrink in proportion when the Workbench narrows
rails or a drawer that present as overlays below a narrow or compact Workbench container breakpoint
transient overlay panels wired with wireWorkbench: collapsed on entering the breakpoint, closed by Escape or an outside press
inline, overlay, or hidden responsive presentation
narrow or compact single-track responsive fill
chrome dividers only while scrolled (wired by wireScrollDividers)
accessibility: Give the Workbench and each meaningful rail or drawer an accessible label.
Give the central region mainLabel when it needs its own named landmark.
Keep collapse controls outside the disappearing region and move focus when a controlled rerender replaces a collapse control with its restore control.

A resizable panel's separator is a focusable role="separator" with its size in aria-valuenow and limits in aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax; arrow keys resize by 16px, Shift+arrow by 64px, and Home/End jump to the limits. It leaves the tab order while its panel is collapsed or not inline.

Given a panel's collapsed signal, wireWorkbench closes an open overlay panel on Escape or an outside press and, however the panel closed, returns focus stranded inside it to the control that opened it, else to its restore control.

An overlay panel can cover the toolbar toggle that opened it (a narrow right rail covers an editor toolbar's trailing toggle), so give every panel that may overlay its own close control in its header: a Pane header Toolbar with a single ToolbarControlGroup around the collapsiblePanelToggleIcon(side, false) button.

notes: Workbench owns the rail and drawer separators; each region's content owns its internal padding and scroll behavior.

stateAttributes.meaning: Present on a resizable rail or the drawer while a pointer drag resizes it.

stateAttributes.meaning: The physical edges, in canonical t/r/b/l order, beyond which content is scrolled out of view; absent when nothing is hidden (content that fits never reports its far edges). Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

stateAttributes.meaning: The sides, in t/r/b/l order, on which this chrome currently draws its scroll divider: the side facing the scroller while content is hidden beyond it. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

entries.name: CollapsiblePanel
entries.description: A standalone controlled left or right rail or bottom drawer with standard collapse icons and optional compact-overlay behavior through wireSidebar.
entries.purpose: Add one independently collapsible peripheral panel without adopting the complete multi-panel Workbench shell.
useWhen: An application needs one collapsible side rail or bottom drawer outside a full Workbench.
The panel should become a dismissable, focus-managed overlay on compact devices.
avoidWhen: Do not use CollapsiblePanel for a complete editor shell with multiple coordinated rails and a drawer; use Workbench.
Do not preserve an empty icon-only rail when collapsed; move the restore control into adjacent visible chrome.

alternatives.when: Use Workbench when the central work area coordinates multiple peripheral panels.
Use the production recipe for collapse, restore, compact overlay, focus, and persistence ownership.

variants: chrome dividers only while scrolled (wired by wireScrollDividers)
accessibility: Give the panel region and every collapse or restore control an accessible label.
Keep the restore control outside the disappearing panel and use wireSidebar for focus transfer, Escape, backdrop dismissal, and compact focus trapping.

notes: The panel owns its dock-edge separator and size track; its child content owns internal padding and scrolling.

stateAttributes.meaning: With a deviceClass on a compact device: "true" for the overlay presentation, "false" for hidden. Absent on a wide device class. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

stateAttributes.name: data-morph-preserve
stateAttributes.meaning: Keeps the injected compact-overlay backdrop through the application's re-render; the helper creates and removes the backdrop itself.

Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

entries.name: SunkenPanel
entries.description: A rounded or square-corner lowered application surface with one compact inset and a vertical content stack.
entries.purpose: Group a vertical list of application content on a visually lowered surface with one owned 8px inset and an explicit rounded or square-corner shape.
useWhen: A main content region or nested work area needs a darker/lowered background and one compact inset around a vertical stack.
Use the default rounded shape for an inset surface; choose square for a flush or edge-to-edge application area.
avoidWhen: Do not use it merely to add padding, as a substitute for Pane anatomy, or around children that already own the same outer surface.

alternatives.when: Use layout roles for pane, toolbar, scroll, and ordinary content-stack ownership.

appOwns: optional keyboard or programmatic focus (tabIndex) and persistent outline (outlined)
accessibility: Pass ariaLabel only when the surface is a distinct named region; otherwise it remains a non-landmark grouping.

notes: The root owns one 8px inset and vertical gap; children own their borders and internal geometry.

entries.name: BackdropImage
entries.description: An image block at the top of a scrolling view that can lag the scroll, fade into an app color, and keep painting that color under the content below.
entries.purpose: Open a scrolling Pane or NavStack view with a hero or tiled backdrop image (an artist, album, or place page) that lags the scroll and progressively blurs on a compositor-only scroll timeline, dissolves through a mask into an app-chosen color, and continues that color under the following content, with Kerf-owned static fallbacks.
useWhen: A scrolling view opens with a large mood or identity image (an artist, album, place, or collection header) whose page should read as one surface with it.
The image should lag the scroll (parallax), blur progressively as it scrolls away, or dissolve into a color without app scroll listeners, animated filters, or background-attachment: fixed.
avoidWhen: Do not use for inline content images, thumbnails, avatars, or media a person inspects; render an img or the matching media component.
Do not hand-roll scroll listeners, background-attachment: fixed, animated blur filters, or mask gradients around an image in app CSS.
Do not put it in a region that does not scroll vertically; parallax needs a scroll container ancestor.

alternatives.when: Place BackdropImage first in a Pane's scrolling content (or a NavStack view) so its scroller drives the parallax.
Use SunkenPanel for a lowered work surface without imagery.

appOwns: the image, its alt text (empty for a decorative image), and responsive candidates
the fade color, whether the image lags the scroll, and whether it blurs (and any pre-blurred asset)
overlay content and its contrast against the image and scrim
whether the image runs up beneath overlay or clear chrome and the top safe area (underChrome); it must then be the first child of the Pane's content
variants: fitted image (cover, contain, fill) with a focal position
parallax none, subtle, or a 0 to 1 lag factor
progressive blur from a once-filtered copy or an app-supplied blurred asset, with an optional dim
fade into a color that also paints below
bottom or full scrim under overlay content
image running beneath clear or overlay chrome (underChrome)
accessibility: alt describes a meaningful image; pass an empty alt for a decorative one. A tiled image with alt text is exposed as role="img". Parallax and the progressive blur run only with prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and scroll-driven animation support, and are off under data-kui-effects="static" and on slow-update displays, leaving a static, sharp image; the blurred copy is decorative and aria-hidden. Reduced transparency or increased contrast replaces the fade with a hard edge on solid fadeTo and puts overlay content on a solid fadeTo band. Overlay text needs a scrim or fade color that keeps it at AA.

notes: The root bleeds to the Pane's resolved inline insets (the safe area) and hands them back to its overlay and content, so their items keep the ordinary text axis.
The image block is height tall (default 320px) and grows with taller overlay content.

entries.name: Toolbar
entries.description: Leading, centered, and trailing toolbar composition.
entries.purpose: Leading, centered, and trailing toolbar composition.
useWhen: Compose application chrome or a page, panel, or dialog heading with leading, center, and trailing regions.
Use typed hideBelow/showBelow lengths with wireToolbarVisibility(root) for per-item toolbar priority; keep primary actions available and provide a showBelow overflow alternative.
avoidWhen: Do not use it as a generic wrapper when no toolbar or heading relationship exists.
appOwns: which screen edges an app bar or bottom bar outside a Pane header or footer claims for device safe areas (safeAreaEdges)
variants: scroll dividers when named as wireScrollDividers targets chrome
stacked zones at compact or narrow widths
content-driven wrap that keeps a heading title whole
center priority for an expanded center control
trailing priority for an expanded trailing control at compact or narrow widths
trailing groups and a standalone primary wa-button wrap instead of clipping
outer inset independently configurable from zone gap
compact density: a 40px header (34px band, 3px block insets) for an embedded panel, filled with compact ToolbarControlGroups
app bar or bottom bar claiming its screen edges (safeAreaEdges)
typed hideBelow/showBelow thresholds at the nearest Toolbar content width
accessibility: Supply a label when the toolbar needs an accessible name.

notes: Padding belongs to the toolbar; --kui-toolbar-inset controls outer padding and minimum height independently of --kui-toolbar-gap. dividerSides selects any canonical combination of its physical top, right, bottom, and left edges.

Safe areas: a Pane header or footer hands a sole Toolbar its inline edges; an app bar or bottom bar at a screen edge claims its sides with safeAreaEdges and pads each claimed side by the --kui-edge-inset-* context or the full device inset, while its box and dividers paint through.

entries.name: ToolbarControlGroup
entries.description: Typed toolbar groups for buttons, semantic action links, compact mixed controls, selected states, dropdown surfaces, and avatar controls.
entries.purpose: Provide complete toolbar action geometry through configuration, including semantic anchors, overflow containment, and dropdown menu insets without application CSS.
useWhen: Group related controls inside a toolbar with a supported visual treatment.
Use ToolbarActionLink for navigation or external resources that must retain native anchor semantics inside a group.

Fill it with plain <button> controls (the group styles > button fully); use wa-button only for a Web Awesome feature. A popup menu is a PopupMenu in a single group with nestedDropdown; it renders its own trigger, so never hand-write wa-dropdown markup. Each control stays whole: an icon sits beside its label on one row and no trigger gets a fixed width. Use overflow=wrap for independent links that should move as whole actions to another row on narrow surfaces.
For an avatar control, set content=avatar and avatarImage instead of inserting an img; one button paints the group and multiple buttons paint only the pressed highlight.
In a Workbench or CollapsiblePanel toolbar, mark a group relocateOnCollapse to keep it available in the work-area toolbar when the panel closes; place it directly or in an array in any toolbar zone.
Use tileTone for a contained single group containing only a direct decorative SVG icon; interactive or mixed groups retain their existing control chrome.

Set material=glass on a group floating over imagery or a clear (transparent) toolbar: it paints the translucent, blurred chrome material with a specular edge, controls keep AA in the normal text color, and the fill turns opaque under reduced transparency, increased contrast, or static effects. Keep the solid default on an opaque toolbar.
Set expandedOverflow=visible on an expanded search to anchor application suggestions, date pickers, or help below the group without overriding its geometry.
Use typed hideBelow/showBelow lengths with wireToolbarVisibility(root) for per-item toolbar priority; keep primary actions available and provide a showBelow overflow alternative.
avoidWhen: Do not use merely to align unrelated buttons or to imitate an exclusive choice.
Do not reach for wa-button for an ordinary control inside the group — a plain <button> is the default and avoids the Web Awesome dependency.

alternatives.when: Outside a Toolbar, a standalone icon-only toggle is an icon-only Button with pressed.

variants: icon, text, mixed, or avatar content
raised, filled, outline, or no selected chrome (group-wide or one control via data-selected-chrome="none")
brand, neutral, or pop selected tone
standard, compact, or list-zero dropdown menu inset
visible, horizontally scrollable, or whole-action wrapping overflow
always visible or compact-only responsive visibility

neutral, brand, success, warning, or danger quiet icon tile tone

A disabled native button (disabled, or aria-disabled="true" when it must stay focusable) dims to half opacity with the not-allowed cursor and no hover surface; a disabled raw wa-button paints no hover surface either. Do not add disabled styling yourself.

Name an icon-only button or link with aria-label, not title. Once any help-tag installer is imported (select/register, popup-menu/register, or help-tags/register), it shows an aria-hidden help tag repeating that name after a 500ms hover and at once on keyboard focus, hidden on a press and on Escape, and never joins aria-labelledby. A native title keeps the browser tooltip and gets no second tag.

In an overlay Pane header (headerPresentation="overlay"), overlay NavStack chrome (chromePresentation="overlay") or bottom toolbar (bottomToolbarPresentation="overlay"), or a DialogSurface floating header's header-actions (headerPresentation="floating"), a default-tone group (not dark-toned, not an avatar scrim) takes --kui-color-text for its controls, so they keep WCAG AA over content passing beneath the translucent chrome material.

A dark-toned group's hover paints a 14% surface wash over its loud fill, on one control of a group or across a lone control's whole group, so the on-loud icon keeps at least 3:1 over a light page and well above it in dark.

entries.name: Surface Scaffolds
entries.description: A native modal dialog (DialogSurface) with Kerf's header, body, and footer chrome, typed preferred widths, viewport bounds, and presentations, plus a non-modal popover dialog and popup inset composition.
entries.purpose: Configure recurring dialog and popup geometry without consumer ::part() overrides.
useWhen: A modal task needs a dialog: render a DialogSurface with a label (or labelledBy plus a heading), its body as children, and its buttons as footer, then open it with openDialog() and close it with closeDialog(), the close button, or any element with data-dialog-close. A raw Web Awesome dropdown that needs a list-compatible menu inset uses PopupSurface.
A dialog body should compose rows, sections, or aligned bare prose through List and ListInsetText.
A modal needs a typed preferred width, viewport gutter, or dynamic viewport-bounded height cap while retaining native body scrolling and footer actions.
A dialog that must leave the page interactive and close on Escape or an outside press uses PopoverDialogSurface; one that fills its body with a SplitView or Pane uses height and bodyLayout="fill".
A chat-style dialog floats its composer over the transcript with footerPresentation="floating" and keeps a heading or notice above one scrolling transcript with bodyLayout="fill-last".

A phone-first task (compose, quick edit, a picker) should rise from the bottom edge as a sheet the person can resize: presentation="bottom-sheet" with height, and resizable with minHeight / maxHeight bounds.

A dialog's title bar should float over the body on the translucent chrome material so a transcript scrolls visibly beneath both the title bar and a floating composer (headerPresentation="floating" with bodyLayout="fill" and a List or Pane that opts into scrollClearance="both").
avoidWhen: Do not use it as a generic layout wrapper, and do not toggle the dialog's open attribute (that opens it non-modally); open and close it with openDialog() and closeDialog().
Do not stack a dialog body inset around children that already own List or content-item geometry; use bodyInset none.

Do not put quiet secondary text of your own in a floating dialog header; it can fall below AA over the content passing beneath. A ToolbarText as the dialog's heading (or in headerActions) is fine: its title takes the normal text color and its description lifts halfway toward it, keeping AA.
appOwns: whether a close request may proceed (cancel kui-request-close to keep the dialog open; the panel pulses)
content, heading, header actions, and footer

whether core kerfjs/overlay dialogs presented as bottom sheets take this package's geometry and slide (import @kerfjs/ui/overlay-sheet.css; exitClass 'kui-overlay-sheet-exit' for the slide out; the kui-overlay-sheet-resizable class plus wireOverlaySheets for a resize grabber)
variants: data-* rootAttributes (a data-key) so sibling dialogs morph by identity
modal, side-sheet, fullscreen, or bottom-sheet dialog

bottom sheet attached to the bottom edge: square bottom corners, safe-area and virtual-keyboard clearance behind the panel, slide (or standard) enter and exit motion, and an optional resizable top grabber bounded by minHeight and maxHeight
typed modal preferred width, viewport gutter, and maximum height, including viewport cap
definite viewport-bounded modal height and a fill body layout for one child
fill-last body layout: fixed rows above one filling, scrolling last child
docked or floating footer with a typed footerOffset; the body reserves the measured footer height
floating footer over a filling child that opts into block-end scrollClearance: content scrolls beneath the footer through the published --kui-scroll-clearance-block-end
docked or floating header (headerPresentation) on the translucent chrome material; the body reserves the measured header height
floating header over a filling only child that opts into block-start scrollClearance: content scrolls beneath the title bar through the published --kui-scroll-clearance-block-start
floating header divider as scroll state: a hairline under the title bar only while the body or a filling child beneath it is scrolled away from its top
non-modal light-dismiss PopoverDialogSurface, overlay or embedded in flow, named by label or labelledBy and described by describedBy
none, compact, or comfortable body and footer inset
standard, compact, or zero-inset popup menu
core kerfjs/overlay confirm/prompt/form/choice as a bottom sheet styled by @kerfjs/ui/overlay-sheet.css
resizable core kerfjs/overlay bottom sheet: the kui-overlay-sheet-resizable class plus wireOverlaySheets adds the resizable DialogSurface sheet grabber
header with label text or heading content, headerActions, a close button, and an optional footer; withoutHeader for content that owns its heading and close control
light dismiss (a backdrop press closes; otherwise the panel pulses)
accessibility: DialogSurface is a native <dialog> opened modally (showModal): it is in the top layer, the rest of the page is inert, focus stays inside, and it returns to the opener on close. Focus starts on an autofocus element, otherwise on the panel.

Name it with label (also its title text) or labelledBy (the id of a heading, such as a ToolbarText). The close button is named Close (closeLabel) and Escape asks to close; the cancelable kui-request-close event reports source close-button, escape, or backdrop.
Name a PopoverDialogSurface with label or labelledBy, and describe it with describedBy (rendered as aria-describedby), usually a title ToolbarText descriptionId.

A floating header's title uses the normal text color, which keeps WCAG AA over the 80% raised chrome material on any content; the material turns opaque under prefers-reduced-transparency, prefers-contrast: more, forced colors, or without backdrop-filter.

A resizable bottom sheet's grabber is a focusable horizontal separator ("Resize sheet") with aria-valuemin, aria-valuenow, and aria-valuemax in visible px; the arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home, and End resize it, and its slide motion is skipped under prefers-reduced-motion.
Use popup surfaces only for real dropdown menus with named triggers.

entries.name: ListDetailDialog
entries.description: A modal list-detail dialog whose list and detail columns each run its full height: the list column carries a secondary title and its own controls, the detail column carries the dialog's primary title, actions, and close control, and compact devices get a full-screen drill-down.
entries.purpose: Present a selectable list beside the selected item's detail inside a modal, with the dialog's title and close control in the detail column and a one-pane drill-down on compact devices.
useWhen: A modal task picks one record from a list and shows its detail beside it (project details, account switcher, settings categories): render ListDetailDialog with list and detail, open it with openDialog(), and pass compact from deviceClass().value.compact.
The dialog's primary title, actions, and close control belong to the selected item's detail rather than spanning both columns, and the column divider should run the dialog's full height.
avoidWhen: Do not use it for a single-pane dialog; use DialogSurface.
Do not compose DialogSurface around a SplitView by hand for this layout; the surface header would span both columns and stop the divider below it.
Do not use it when the task needs a durable route or more working space than a modal; use a page with SplitView.

alternatives.when: Use DialogSurface for a single-pane dialog.
Use SplitView for the same list-detail flow as a page rather than a modal.
Use WorkbenchDialog for an editing task with side panels.

appOwns: selected item and, on compact devices, detailActive and the back action (nav-back)
list and detail content, their titles, toolbar controls, and footers
variants: roomy modal: a full-height list column and a full-height detail column with a fixed list width (default 280px, at most 40% of the dialog)
list column header controls and a pinned list footer
detail header actions before the close control, a description under the title, and a pinned detail footer
compact full-screen NavStack drill-down with the close control on every view
definite height (default 560px) or a viewport height cap, viewport gutter, size or preferred width, and light dismiss
accessibility: It is a native modal <dialog> named by label: the page is inert, focus stays inside, Escape asks to close, and focus returns to the opener on close.
On roomy devices the detail title is a level-2 heading; every presentation keeps a close control named Close (closeLabel), and the compact back control is named by backLabel.

notes: The dialog draws no header and no body inset; each column is a Pane that owns its chrome and content insets, and the column divider runs the dialog's full height.

entries.name: WorkbenchDialog
entries.description: A modal workbench dialog: a header-less DialogSurface whose body is a Workbench. The work area's toolbar carries the dialog's primary title, actions, and close control; side rails keep their own toolbars and run the dialog's full height; compact devices get a full-screen dialog whose rails open as overlays over the work area.
entries.purpose: Present an editing task with side panels (layers, an inspector) inside a modal, with the dialog's title and close control in the work area and rails that overlay the work area on compact devices instead of narrowing it.
useWhen: A modal editing task needs a work area with side panels (a slide or record editor with layers and an inspector): render WorkbenchDialog with main and leftRail/rightRail, open it with openDialog(), pass compact from deviceClass().value.compact, and wire wireWorkbench on the Workbench id (<id>-workbench) with each rail's collapsed signal.
On compact devices the rails should start hidden and open as overlays from toolbar toggles, keeping the work area's width.
avoidWhen: Do not use it for a single-pane dialog; use DialogSurface.
Do not use it to pick a record from a list beside its detail; use ListDetailDialog.
Do not compose DialogSurface around a Workbench by hand for this layout; the surface header would span the rails and the close control would not follow a hidden rail's toggle.
Do not use it when the task needs a durable route; use a page with Workbench.

alternatives.when: Use ListDetailDialog to pick a record from a list and show its detail.
Use DialogSurface for a single-pane dialog.
Use Workbench for the same layout as a page rather than a modal.

appOwns: device-class policy (compact), and starting the rails collapsed on compact devices
each rail's collapsed state and toggle actions (wireWorkbench closes an overlay rail on Escape or an outside press)
the work area, rail content, actions, and bottom toolbar
variants: roomy modal: full-height left and right rails with their own toolbars beside the work area
a hidden rail's toggle relocates into the work area's toolbar, before the close control
work-area leading groups, actions, a description under the title, a fixed footer, and a bottom toolbar
a bottom drawer under the work area
compact full-screen dialog with overlay rails that start hidden
definite height (default 560px) or a height cap, viewport gutter, size or preferred width, and light dismiss
accessibility: It is a native modal <dialog> named by label: the page is inert, focus stays inside, Escape asks to close, and focus returns to the opener on close.

The title is a level-2 heading; the close control is named Close (closeLabel) and stays the outermost trailing control. An open overlay rail takes focus, keeps Tab inside it, and closes on Escape before the dialog does.

notes: The dialog draws no header and no body inset; the Workbench's work area and rails own their chrome and content insets, and the rail dividers run the dialog's full height.

stateAttributes.name: data-responsive-overlay-active
stateAttributes.meaning: Present while a panel's numeric responsiveOverlayAt threshold applies to the Workbench width; the same measurement drives overlay layout and collapsed-state transitions.

stateAttributes.name: data-numeric-overlays
stateAttributes.meaning: Space-separated left, right, drawer, rail-open, and open tokens mirror numeric overlay state for local CSS invalidation. Absent when no numeric overlay is active.

stateAttributes.name: data-handle-inset
stateAttributes.meaning: Written by the shared resize wiring when the work-area minimum or a parent clamp holds a rail's maximum near its size. It carries no Workbench styling; the Workbench handle stays at the rail's inner edge.

stateAttributes.name: data-resizing
stateAttributes.meaning: Present on a resizable rail or the drawer while a pointer drag resizes it.

entries.name: FloatingToolbar
entries.description: A transparent, forced-dark toolbar that floats over its container's content.
entries.purpose: A transparent, forced-dark toolbar that floats over its container's content.
useWhen: Float a small cluster of controls (e.g. a drawer restore) over scrolling content without covering dialogs.
avoidWhen: Do not use for a primary page or panel toolbar, or for anything that must sit above overlays (it is not top-layer).
accessibility: Give the toolbar an accessible name (label is required — it exposes role="toolbar").

entries.name: ToolbarText
entries.description: Extra-large through extra-small toolbar identity text.
entries.purpose: Extra-large through extra-small toolbar identity text.
useWhen: Render toolbar identity or heading text at a supported hierarchy size; pass headingLevel for heading semantics.
Use action for an editable toolbar title: it renders a native button that shrinks and ellipsizes beside sibling status chips.
Use tone=dark for title or filename text on a loud toolbar surface, matching dark ToolbarControlGroups.
Use typed hideBelow/showBelow lengths with wireToolbarVisibility(root) for per-item toolbar priority; keep primary actions available and provide a showBelow overflow alternative.
avoidWhen: Do not omit headingLevel when the text is the page or section heading.

Large, default, and small are intentionally quiet toolbar identity text in default tone. Use xlarge-fixed for a normal-color toolbar heading at the fixed font-l step; use Text with an h2-h6 variant for a content subsection title, or ListHeader for a list or menu section.

alternatives.when: Use Text variant h2-h6 for a normal-color subsection title in content rather than toolbar identity.
Use ListHeader for a list or menu section label with a count, badge, action, or disclosure.

appOwns: the delegated action handler and display-to-input editing swap
variants: description: quiet single-line supporting copy under a read-only title, aligned with its text, with descriptionId for aria-describedby
typed hideBelow/showBelow thresholds at the nearest Toolbar content width
accessibility: Plain text is not a heading; pass headingLevel to expose role=heading + aria-level for a page/section title.
Actionable text is a native button with its full text as its accessible name; action cannot be combined with headingLevel, placeholder, or wrap.

In a Pane header with headerPresentation="overlay" or NavStack chrome with chromePresentation="overlay" (or its bottom toolbar with bottomToolbarPresentation="overlay"), or slotted as the label (or into header-actions) of a DialogSurface header with headerPresentation="floating", untoned text keeps WCAG AA over the translucent chrome material: the title takes --kui-color-text at every size and the description mixes --kui-color-text-quiet halfway toward it.

stateAttributes.name: data-toolbar-width-hidden
stateAttributes.on: ToolbarText, ToolbarControlGroup and its paired busy status
stateAttributes.meaning: True when typed hideBelow/showBelow thresholds hide this item at the nearest Toolbar content width. Re-applied after rendering; disposal restores prior markers.

stateAttributes.name: data-toolbar-visibility-probe
stateAttributes.on: private aria-hidden measurement boxes under Toolbar
stateAttributes.meaning: Internal out-of-flow CSS length resolver; created and removed by wireToolbarVisibility.

stateAttributes.name: data-morph-preserve
stateAttributes.on: private aria-hidden measurement boxes and visibility state children
stateAttributes.meaning: Keeps helper-owned geometry and state across Kerf renders; replacement and explicit removal are repaired, and disposal removes them.

stateAttributes.name: data-toolbar-visibility-state
stateAttributes.on: private hidden children of width-managed items and paired busy statuses
stateAttributes.meaning: Preserves actual CSS visibility while rendering removes a transient parent marker, preventing geometry-driven render feedback.

entries.name: Text
entries.description: Semantic native text plus a FieldLabel heading for read-only field previews that matches themed Web Awesome form labels.
entries.purpose: Render paragraph semantics by default, h1 through h6 when selected, or geometry-free inline secondary text as a span while independently configuring quiet or danger tone, compact through extra-large size, or monospace font.
useWhen: Render ordinary application headings or paragraphs with native document semantics, or inline secondary text inside rows, labels, and table cells.
Render FieldLabel over a read-only or click-to-edit preview that replaces a Web Awesome form control.
avoidWhen: Do not use Text for toolbar identity or title content; use ToolbarText inside a Toolbar zone.
Do not choose a heading variant for visual size alone; preserve the document heading hierarchy.
appOwns: FieldLabel copy, preview/edit state, and aria-labelledby association
variants: p, h1 through h6, or inline span semantic variant
compact, default, large, or xlarge size
flush item geometry and tight line height
align start (default), center, or end for centered status copy or trailing values
controlMargins selects exterior 8px gutters with canonical physical Sides
wrap normal, anywhere, nowrap, or truncate; truncate places its ellipsis at the end, the start (keeping the tail), or the middle (keeping the last path segment or a character suffix)
accessibility: Text renders a native paragraph by default; choose an h1 through h6 variant by document outline rather than appearance, or span for inline secondary text.
Ordinary global, data, and ARIA attributes pass through to the native element.
Choose tone, size, and font independently of the heading level so appearance does not distort the document outline.
FieldLabel is plain text, not a native label; give it an id and associate the preview group with aria-labelledby.
Start and middle truncation clip visually only: the whole value stays in the DOM in reading order, and Text shows it as the element's title unless the app supplies one.

notes: Block Text variants reset native margins and add a 1px transparent border plus the standard 8px item padding; flush removes the border and padding. Tight line height is available for compact copy. Span has no margin by default, border, or padding. FieldLabel mirrors the themed Web Awesome label typography, 9px inline inset, and bottom gap.

controlMargins adds the shared control gutter outside selected physical edges without changing border or padding; avoid duplicating a parent inset. Spans retain inline display and native inline margin behavior.

entries.name: Headers
entries.description: Page, dialog, and definition-list hierarchy.
entries.purpose: Page, dialog, and definition-list hierarchy.
useWhen: Compose page, dialog, and definition-list hierarchy from their distinct primitives.
avoidWhen: Do not reuse one header primitive only because its typography looks similar.
accessibility: Preserve heading and description relationships for the containing surface.

entries.name: ValueTable
entries.description: Key/value rows with optional icons.
entries.purpose: Key/value rows with optional icons and aligned separators.
useWhen: Present read-only label/value facts as a semantic definition list, optionally with a 24px leading icon.
avoidWhen: Do not use for editable fields or row/column tabular data.

alternatives.when: Use FramedList for rows of arbitrary content (copy and controls) in the same frame.

variants: stack below a compact or narrow table width
accessibility: Name ValueTable with its label; ValueTableRow supplies dt/dd semantics, and row icons stay decorative unless meaning requires an accessible label.

entries.name: FramedList
entries.description: An inset-grouped list: one rounded, bordered frame with dividers between rows of arbitrary content.
entries.purpose: Group settings-style rows of arbitrary content (copy, keycaps, controls) in one framed surface with between-row dividers and an optional highlighted row, without app list CSS.
useWhen: Settings rows, account or source cards, or shortcut lists group several rows of arbitrary content in one framed surface.
avoidWhen: Do not use for read-only label/value facts; use ValueTable.
Do not use for selectable navigation rows; use List with ListItem.
Do not pad or border its rows from application CSS; FramedListRow owns the inset and divider.

alternatives.when: Use ValueTable when every row is a label and a value.
Use List with ListItem for navigation or selectable rows.

accessibility: Renders a list (ul role=list, li rows); pass label when no heading names it. Highlight is visual; carry its meaning in row content or a control's state.

notes: Rows own the 8px inset and the inset 1px divider above them; the frame owns the 8px margin, border, and radius.

entries.name: SummaryRow
entries.description: A selectable, focusable summary of one item as a list row or a board card, with a state rail, a clamped title, trailing meta, and a metadata line.
entries.purpose: Present dense item summaries (tickets, tasks, messages) as selectable list rows or board cards with Kerf-owned selection, hover, focus, rail, clamping, list-edge rounding, and narrow compaction, without app row CSS.
useWhen: A list or board shows many items as dense, selectable summaries with an identifier, a title, a timestamp, and metadata.
avoidWhen: Do not use for navigation rows with a single label; use ListItem.
Do not use for selectable tiles of free-form content; use ContentItem with selectionMode.
Do not hand-roll row chrome (selection fill, rail, title clamp, edge rounding) in app CSS.

alternatives.when: Use ListItem for navigation rows.
Use ContentItem for selectable rich tiles.

appOwns: the listbox container, selection set, and keyboard movement
the title, leading glyph, trailing meta, and metadata content
variants: list edge start, end, or only
accessibility: Each SummaryRow is role=option with tabindex=0 and aria-selected; place rows in a labeled role=listbox and move focus with the arrow keys in the app. The rail is decorative; carry its meaning in text.

notes: Rows sit flush in a list section and round only the corners at its edges; cards are borderless rounded cards.

entries.name: Row
entries.description: A horizontal flex row with physical-axis alignment, side-selectable text/control insets, a typed xs gap by default, flex participation, and opt-in wrapping.
entries.purpose: Arrange related content horizontally with consistent spacing, optional physical-side text/control insets, and explicit left/center/right/full plus top/middle/bottom/full/baseline alignment instead of application-owned flex wrappers.
useWhen: Arrange a group of sibling components horizontally.
Choose physical horizontal distribution and vertical alignment without writing one-off flex CSS.
Use a finite flex keyword or the flex() builder when Row participates in a flexible parent layout.
Allow a bounded group to wrap while retaining the same typed gap and alignment contract.
Apply the standard text or control inset to selected physical sides without an application wrapper.
avoidWhen: Do not use Row when content belongs in a semantic list or when a named-zone component such as Toolbar owns the composition.
Do not pass raw CSS strings to gap or flex, mix their distinct grammars, or use s/xl spacing steps without a deliberate exception.
Do not use alignment to replace semantic grouping or responsive relocation.

alternatives.when: Use List when the main layout axis is vertical.
Use Toolbar when content belongs to named leading, center, and trailing application-chrome zones.

variants: left/center/right/full horizontal alignment with l/c/r/f and flex aliases
top/middle/bottom/full vertical alignment with t/m/c/b/f and flex aliases, plus baseline alignment
boolean, finite-keyword, or typed CssFlex flex
top/right/bottom/left text and control inset combinations
fill: the layout root fills a definite-height parent
rootAttributes: safe data-*, aria-*, and structural role metadata on the root
accessibility: Row adds layout only and no grouping role; children retain responsibility for native or ARIA semantics.
Wrapping must preserve a readable source and focus order.

notes: Row adds no margin or border. textInsets adds the full 17px content inset and controlInsets adds 8px on selected physical sides; text wins when both select a side.

entries.name: Grid
entries.description: Equal-width columns with a fixed count or a minimum-width responsive mode, typed gaps, physical-side text/control insets, and optional flex participation.
entries.purpose: Arrange related siblings in equal-width columns with either a fixed count or automatic container-width collapse.
useWhen: Arrange related siblings into a fixed positive number of equal-width columns.
Fit equal-width columns down to a typed minimum and collapse as the container narrows.
Prevent wider intrinsic content from making one fractional track wider than its peers.
Use a finite flex keyword or the flex() builder when Grid participates in a flexible parent layout.
avoidWhen: Do not use Grid for intrinsic, asymmetric, spanning, or masonry tracks; use application-owned CSS grid.
Do not use Grid when columns need a user-operable separator; use ResizableRegion.
Do not combine fixed columns with minColumnWidth; choose one layout mode.
Do not pass raw CSS strings to gap or flex, mix their distinct grammars, or use s/xl spacing steps without a deliberate exception.

alternatives.when: Use Row for one horizontal flex line, alignment, or wrapping rather than fixed equal tracks.
Use List when the main layout axis is vertical.
Use ResizableRegion when people must adjust the boundary between tracks.
Use ColumnTrack for a board of columns that scroll sideways or page instead of wrapping.

appOwns: fixed column count or responsive minimum width
typed gap, flex, and physical-side inset choices
variants: typed minimum column width with automatic container-width collapse
boolean, finite-keyword, or typed CssFlex flex
top/right/bottom/left text and control inset combinations
fill: the layout root fills a definite-height parent
rootAttributes: safe data-* metadata on the root
selectionMode=multiple: labeled multi-select grid for ContentItem tiles
accessibility: Grid adds no role by default; selectionMode=multiple requires ariaLabel and supplies a multi-select grid for ContentItem row/gridcell tiles.
wireContentItems uses rendered tile positions for Left/Right/Up/Down and reaches the first or last tile with Home/End.
Responsive column-count changes preserve source and focus order.

notes: textInsets adds 17px and controlInsets adds 8px on selected physical sides; text wins on overlap.
Fixed tracks use minmax(0, 1fr); responsive tracks use auto-fit with a minimum width capped at 100%, preserving equal distribution without narrow overflow.

entries.name: ColumnTrack
entries.description: A horizontal track of equal, min-width columns that scrolls sideways, or pages one column at a time with peek and snapping.
entries.purpose: Lay out a board of columns (kanban) as one horizontal scroll owner: equal columns that never shrink below a minimum, or a paged phone layout with a peeking next column and start snapping, without app track CSS.
useWhen: A board shows several parallel columns (kanban lanes) that must keep a readable width and scroll sideways, or page one at a time on a phone.
avoidWhen: Do not use for a responsive grid that wraps; use Grid.
Do not use for two resizable panes; use SplitView or ResizableRegion.
Do not re-track a Grid from application CSS to get overflowing columns.

alternatives.when: Use Grid when columns should wrap or collapse instead of scrolling.

appOwns: choosing scroll or paged layout (for example by device class)
variants: scroll with a minimum column width
paged with peek and mandatory snapping
accessibility: Name the track with aria-label through rootAttributes when it is a landmark-like region; give each column a region name. Paged scrolling is smooth unless reduced motion is preferred.

notes: The track pads 8px inline and fills its parent's height; columns sit flush and own their insets and vertical scrolling.

entries.name: ContentSwap
entries.description: Two content sides sharing one cell, swapped in place with a push, a crossfade, or no motion.
entries.purpose: Swap arbitrary content in place (a dialog body that steps to a second page, a label or footer whose actions change) with Kerf-owned push or crossfade motion, reduced-motion handling, and an inert, hidden inactive side.
useWhen: A region swaps between two contents in place, such as a dialog's two steps or a footer's action sets, and the change should read as motion.
avoidWhen: Do not use for full navigation views with their own toolbars; use NavStack.
Do not use to swap more than two states at once; render the current pair.
Do not hand-roll stacked cells, inert handling, or push keyframes in app CSS.

alternatives.when: Use NavStack for full views with toolbars and back navigation.

appOwns: which side is active and the push direction
accessibility: The inactive side is inert and aria-hidden; label makes the swap a named region. Push mirrors in right-to-left documents. Reduced motion replaces the slide with a short fade.

notes: Both sides share one grid cell; the region keeps the active side's height and clips the motion.

entries.name: Spacer
