entries.description: A decorative, non-shrinking fixed gap or flexible main-axis spacer with typed physical width and height.
entries.purpose: Express an intentional empty dimension or consume remaining flex space without application-owned spacer markup or raw CSS lengths.
useWhen: Reserve a fixed empty width or height from the UI spacing scale inside a layout.
Push siblings to opposite ends of a Row or other flex container by passing flex.
Use a typed CssLength when the finite spacing scale cannot express the required dimension.
avoidWhen: Do not use Spacer for ordinary rhythm between siblings; prefer Row.gap or List.gap so the parent owns repeated spacing.
Do not use Spacer to compensate for component-owned padding, margin, alignment, or responsive layout defects.
Do not pass raw CSS strings to width or height.

alternatives.when: Use Row.gap when every horizontal sibling needs the same repeated separation.
Use List.gap when every vertical sibling needs the same repeated separation.

appOwns: whether the empty space carries structural meaning
whether the spacer fills the flex main axis
variants: fixed typed CssLength width and/or height
accessibility: Spacer is always decorative and hidden from the accessibility tree.
Spacer must not contain content or become an interaction target.

notes: A fixed Spacer does not shrink. flex changes its flex shorthand from 0 0 auto to 1 1 auto; width and height remain physical dimensions.

entries.name: List
entries.description: A vertical stack with physical-axis alignment, side-selectable text/control insets, optional typed token/length gap, flex growth, vertical scrolling, and independently selectable divider edges.
entries.purpose: Standardize vertical component layout, optional physical-side text/control insets, and scroll/divider ownership instead of repeating ad-hoc flex-column wrappers.
useWhen: Arrange component rows or sections in a vertical stretch-aligned stack.
Let one bounded list own vertical scrolling, flex growth, or one or more physical-edge dividers.
Choose a finite gap shorthand such as xs or m, or compose a typed length with @kerfjs/ui/css-values when the spacing scale is insufficient.
Use a finite flex keyword or the flex() builder when List participates in flexible layout.
Apply the standard text or control inset to selected physical sides without an application wrapper.
Align children horizontally or distribute them vertically with the same physical alignment vocabulary as Row.
Use selectionMode="multiple" and ariaLabel to group selectable rich ContentItem rows in a multi-select grid.

Use scrollClearance on the scrollable List that reaches an edge overlaid by chrome (a DialogSurface floating footer) so rows scroll visibly beneath it while the first and last rows still rest clear of it.
Render a bounded, framed result picker of ListItem rows (search results, duplicate candidates) with scrollable, frame, and typed maxHeight/minHeight instead of an app-owned bordered scroller.

Call wireListFocusScroll(root) once when keyboard users move focus through a scrollable List's rows, so Firefox and Safari bring a partly hidden focused row and its ring fully into view as Chromium does.
Cap and center a page-level content column (a settings page or setup form) with contentWidth and, for long prose, inset="document", instead of an application max-width wrapper.
avoidWhen: Do not use List as semantic list markup; use ul/ol when list semantics are required and apply layout deliberately.
Do not create nested scroll owners or use divider sides as a substitute for meaningful grouping.
Do not pass raw CSS strings to gap or flex, mix their distinct grammars, or use the off-rhythm s/xl spacing steps without a deliberate exception.
appOwns: the bounded height needed for scrolling
typed gap, flex, alignment, and divider choices
the accessible label and selection state of a multi-select grid
which one scroller opts into scroll clearance (the one reaching the covered edge)
the result picker bounds (maxHeight/minHeight) and its rows
variants: boolean, finite-keyword, or typed CssFlex flex
scrollClearance block-start, block-end, or both: clears overlaying chrome inside the scroll area
frame: 1px neutral border, control radius, and a 4px focus-ring-safe inset
typed CssLength maxHeight and minHeight bounds
top/right/bottom/left text and control inset combinations
fill: the layout root fills a definite-height parent
rootAttributes: safe data-*, aria-*, and structural role on the root
scroll dividers when named as wireScrollDividers targets chrome
multi-select grid for rich ContentItem rows
contentWidth (compact 440px, medium 640px, wide 864px) and contentAlign for a readable, centered page column
accessibility: List adds layout only and no list role by default; selectionMode="multiple" makes it an aria-multiselectable grid with a required ariaLabel for selectable ContentItem rows.
Give a scrollable List a bounded block size and keep keyboard focus visible as its contents scroll.
A focused scrollable List (a keyboard-focusable scroller) draws the theme focus ring inset and rounded inside its own box, so a rounded or clipping parent never cuts it off; do not restyle its focus.

With wireListFocusScroll, a keyboard-focused (:focus-visible) element in a scrollable List whose focus ring crosses the clip is scrolled into view (block and inline nearest, honoring the ring-room scroll padding) in every engine; pointer focus never scrolls, so a click cannot move its row from under the pointer.

notes: List adds no margin. dividerSides draws selected physical edges without changing geometry; textInsets adds the full 17px content inset and controlInsets adds 8px on selected sides, with text winning on overlap.

scrollClearance adds the inherited --kui-scroll-clearance-block-start/end context, published by overlaying chrome, to the List block padding and scroll-padding on the opted-in edges; without it the context is ignored.

frame draws a 1px --kui-color-neutral-border-normal border with --kui-radius-m and a 4px --kui-space-2xs inset on every side (replacing inset/textInsets/controlInsets), exactly the focus-ring reach, so the first and last rows' rings stay inside the clip at the scroll extremes; maxHeight/minHeight bound the List directly.

Every scrollable List's block scroll padding is the focus-ring reach plus 2px of slack (6px, no change at rest), so any row focused or scrolled into view stops with its ring inside the clip; an unframed List's first and last rows still meet the clip at the scroll extremes, so use frame when they must show a whole ring.

As a direct child of a Pane's scrolling content, a List that does not scroll itself never shrinks below its rows (flex-shrink 0), so the content's block-end padding (a bottom safe area, an overlay NavStack bottom toolbar's clearance) follows its last row.

stateAttributes.name: data-scroll-overflow
stateAttributes.meaning: The physical edges, in canonical t/r/b/l order, beyond which content is scrolled out of view; absent when nothing is hidden (content that fits never reports its far edges). Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

stateAttributes.name: data-scroll-divider
stateAttributes.on: a List named as targets chrome
stateAttributes.meaning: The sides, in t/r/b/l order, on which this chrome currently draws its scroll divider: the side facing the scroller while content is hidden beyond it. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

stateAttributes.name: data-header-overlay
stateAttributes.meaning: measured once the wiring has measured a Pane's overlay header (headerPresentation: overlay) and published its border-box height as --kui-scroll-clearance-block-start on the Pane root, plus a classic content scrollbar's inline size as --kui-pane-scrollbar-inline-size, which the header leaves uncovered. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

entries.name: ListHeader
entries.description: Configurable section headings with five independent label sizes, full-width or shrink-wrapped inline presentation, semantic count/status indicators, density, group dividers, a logical-end action, disclosure states, and protected native-popover trigger metadata.
entries.purpose: Fill the available section width by default, or shrink-wrap without outer geometry when inline, while splitting a dormant title and optional count or combined badge/status indicators from a logical-end action with an 18px visual; disclosure mode renders the title cluster as a button with a default production DisclosureArrow.
useWhen: Label a navigation section with an optional semantic count or simultaneous badge and status indicators, plus an action or disclosure state; toggle mode supplies an 18px DisclosureArrow unless actionIcon replaces it.
avoidWhen: Do not concatenate a section count into label or pass a bare number through badge; use count with its required localized countLabel for a sole section quantity.
Do not use as a page or dialog title.
appOwns: valid count and localized count label
optional status content alongside badge, including conditional undefined values
variants: label sizes xs, sm (default), m, l, xl
neutral, accent, pop, or danger indicator tone
before, after, or paired group divider
accessibility: A valid count is hidden as duplicate visual text and its required localized countLabel joins the owned heading or disclosure-button accessible name; zero remains visible.

The application controls and updates disclosure state and the revealed content; the default DisclosureArrow mirrors expanded while the button name stays stable. triggerAttributes can describe the controlled relationship but cannot replace the owned accessible name or expanded state.

entries.name: ListActionRow
entries.description: Configurable navigation rows with structured labels, status/busy metadata, density, group dividers, and a primary native-button action beside a sibling trailing native button or trailing overflow PopupMenu.
entries.purpose: Keep a selectable primary row action and an independently named trailing action as sibling native controls inside one noninteractive visual row.
useWhen: A navigation or item row needs both a primary selectable action and an independently focusable trailing action.
A command row needs a trailing "…" overflow menu (trailingMenu), optionally also opened at the pointer from the row's contextmenu with openPopupMenuAt.
A settings or command row identifies each entry by a colored icon tile (iconTile) instead of a bare glyph.
avoidWhen: Use ListItem when trailing content is dormant metadata; use TabBarItem only for tablist semantics and ToolbarControlGroup only for toolbar controls.
Do not inject declaration strings; use className, public tokens, and cataloged component props for application styling.

alternatives.when: Trailing content is noninteractive.
The primary control selects a tabpanel inside TabBar.

variants: before, after, or paired group divider
position-aware divided-list corners: flat wherever a divider line (this row's or a neighbor's) meets the edge
draggable row with dragging and drop-before / drop-after insertion states
filled leading icon tile (iconTile): a quiet tone preset (neutral, brand, success, warning, danger) or an application fill with an optional foreground; a 32px rounded tile holding an 18px glyph
accessibility: The noninteractive root contains two sibling native buttons in primary-then-trailing focus order; each button has its own action, item identity, accessible name, and disabled state.

A trailingMenu replaces the trailing button with a PopupMenu trigger in the same position: an icon-only button named by trailingMenu.label that exposes aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded, moves focus into the menu, and returns focus to the trigger on Escape or a choice.

Selection semantics are exposed only by the primary button; label, icon, and trailingActionIcon are dormant SafeHtml and must not contain interactive descendants; never place an interactive descendant in ListItem.trailing.

A draggable row is dragged by its noninteractive root; with wireListReorder, Alt+Shift+ArrowUp/ArrowDown on its primary button moves it, and focus returns to that button after the application re-renders.

stateAttributes.name: data-dragging
stateAttributes.meaning: "true" on every row a pointer drag is moving (the dragged row, or every selected row of its list when the dragged row is selected). Same attribute the `dragging` prop renders.

stateAttributes.name: data-drop-position
stateAttributes.meaning: "before" or "after": the edge of this row the dragged rows would land beside. Same attribute the `dropPosition` prop renders.

entries.name: ListItem
entries.description: Configurable native-button action rows and native-anchor navigation rows with structured labels, status/busy metadata, density, group dividers, protected domain metadata hooks, and rounded-boundary overflow clipping.
entries.purpose: Selectable, disabled, trailing, and multiline action or link rows.
useWhen: Render a selectable, disabled, trailing, or multiline sidebar action row whose descendants must remain clipped to the rounded row boundary; use ListItemLink when the destination has an href and needs native link activation.
A settings or command row identifies each entry by a colored icon tile (iconTile) instead of a bare glyph.
avoidWhen: Do not use for an ordinary inline link, form button, isolated ARIA menuitem, or an interactive trailing action; use ListActionRow for sibling row actions.
Do not inject declaration strings; use className, public tokens, and cataloged component props for application styling.

alternatives.when: The trailing region must be independently interactive.
Use SummaryRow for dense selectable item summaries with metadata.

variants: centered icon beside a multiline label
draggable row with dragging and drop-before / drop-after insertion states
before, after, or paired group divider
position-aware divided-list corners: flat wherever a divider line (this row's or a neighbor's) meets the edge
filled leading icon tile (iconTile): a quiet tone preset (neutral, brand, success, warning, danger) or an application fill with an optional foreground; a 32px rounded tile holding an 18px glyph
accessibility: ListItem uses native button activation and pressed maps to aria-pressed; ListItemLink uses native anchor activation and external opens a new tab with safe rel and an announced default label. Both map selected to aria-current; disabled or loading links omit href and leave the tab order. rootAttributes cannot add role=menuitem or replace owned ARIA; trailing is dormant content and must not contain controls. A draggable row reorders by pointer drag or, with wireListReorder, Alt+Shift+ArrowUp/ArrowDown; a placeholder is never draggable.

notes: Public resting, hover, and selected text, fill, and border tokens can be scoped to a row or its containing list without changing the default tones.

stateAttributes.name: data-dragging
stateAttributes.meaning: "true" on every row a pointer drag is moving (the dragged row, or every selected row of its list when the dragged row is selected). Same attribute the `dragging` prop renders.

stateAttributes.name: data-drop-position
stateAttributes.on: ListItem / ListItemLink row under the pointer
stateAttributes.meaning: "before" or "after": the edge of this row the dragged rows would land beside. Same attribute the `dropPosition` prop renders.

entries.name: ListInsetControl
entries.description: Insets selected physical sides of a self-bordered control in a pane/list content region.
entries.purpose: Apply the standard 8px outer margin to all physical sides of a self-bordered control by default, or only the sides selected with the canonical Sides contract.
useWhen: Place a control that carries its own border and padding (an input, a wa-* control) in a pane/list content region so its edges align with .kui-content items.
avoidWhen: Do not wrap a component that already owns its content-item margin (ListItem, StateBanner, …) — that double-insets it. Use ListInsetText for bare text.
appOwns: the wrapped control and its behavior
accessibility: A layout wrapper only; it adds no role or name — the wrapped control keeps its own.

entries.name: ListInsetText
entries.description: Gives selected physical sides of bare text the content-item geometry so it lines up with bordered items.
entries.purpose: Apply the full 8px margin + 1px transparent border + 8px padding to all physical sides of bare text by default, or only the sides selected with the canonical Sides contract.
useWhen: Line a plain text element up with bordered .kui-content items — it adds the 8px margin, 1px transparent border, and 8px padding the text lacks.
avoidWhen: Do not use it to wrap an interactive control (use ListInsetControl), or a component that already owns its content-item geometry.
accessibility: A layout wrapper only; it adds no role or name.

entries.name: ContentItem
entries.description: One self-contained content child with shared geometry plus typed transparent, surface, or semantic appearance, frame, and shape choices.
entries.purpose: Render one self-contained .kui-content child that owns its 8px inline margin, real 1px border, 8px padding, radius, and optional coordinated surface colors.
useWhen: An ordinary surface-like child of a Pane or .kui-content stack needs the shared content-item geometry so its content edge lands at the standard 17px inset.
A content item marks a real distinction and must read as visibly bounded: pass frame="framed" (the border is always reserved, so geometry does not change).
A content item needs the base surface or a coordinated semantic status treatment: pass appearance="surface" or a semantic appearance such as success or danger.
A content item should follow a pill control's 22px radius: pass shape="pill".
A selectable rich card needs nested controls: use selectionMode="multiple" inside a labeled List multi-select grid.
avoidWhen: Do not wrap a component that already owns content-item geometry (ListItem, ListHeader, StateBanner, Toolbar, ValueTable) or pad around a ContentItem; either double-insets.
Do not frame an item only to make it look contained; hierarchy comes from alignment, spacing, and type first.
Do not use its surface appearance for a lowered inset panel around a stack; use SunkenPanel for that structure.
Do not use it for bare text alone; use ListInsetText, which adds the same inset without claiming a surface.

alternatives.when: Use ListInsetText when bare text only needs to align with neighboring content items.
Use SunkenPanel for a lowered, filled surface around a vertical stack.
Place ContentItem children in a Pane or .kui-content stack, which owns the 24px major rhythm.

appOwns: whether the item marks a real distinction that warrants a visible frame
whether the item needs a surface or semantic appearance
whether the item is a programmatic focus target
optional static-item Tab stop and persistent focus outline
the selection set and Shift/Cmd extension for multi-select rich cards
variants: neutral, info, pop, success, warning, or danger semantic item
brand-loud item (solid brand fill, on-loud foreground)
chat bubble at the start or end of the row (bubble), fit to its content up to 80%
gridRow: a non-selectable row (role="row" with a gridcell) between selectable rows of a multi-select List or Grid
accessibility: An ordinary item adds no role or name; pass ariaLabel only when the item is a distinct named region (it then renders role="region").
focusTarget makes the item a programmatic focus target (tabindex="-1", never a tab stop), such as a NavStack view's data-nav-focus target.
The frame is decorative and never the only signal of state.

selectionMode="multiple" renders a focusable row with aria-selected and a gridcell for nested controls; place it in a labeled List selectionMode="multiple" grid. wireContentItems moves focus among rows with Up/Down and Home/End while nested controls retain those keys. Enter and Space activate the card with a click that carries the key's Shift, Ctrl, and Cmd state, so one delegated click handler implements range and toggle selection for pointer and keyboard alike. Guard the app's delegated card action with isContentItemActivation so a nested control does not select the row.

In a multi-select List or Grid, wireContentItems keeps one roving Tab stop (the last focused row, else the first selected, else the first enabled) across re-renders. A gridRow item is a row with a gridcell and no aria-selected or Tab stop; arrow keys skip it and its controls stay reachable by Tab.

notes: The 1px border is always reserved; transparent items paint it only when frame="framed", while surface and semantic appearances coordinate its color with their background and foreground.

entries.name: Disclosure
entries.description: Content a person shows and hides under a summary row: a native details element with a DisclosureArrow, a title, and an optional quiet detail, on content-item geometry, with plain, framed, and sunken appearances and native exclusive (accordion) groups.
entries.purpose: Keep secondary or optional content one press away under a summary, or let a person open one of several sections at a time.
useWhen: Optional or advanced content should stay out of the way until a person asks for it (advanced settings, a build log, release notes).
A list of questions or sections should open one at a time: give the Disclosures the same name for a native exclusive accordion.
avoidWhen: Do not use it to switch between peer views; use a SegmentedControl or TabBar.
Do not use it for primary navigation or a collapsible sidebar; use a List or CollapsiblePanel.
Do not hand-build a details element with its own marker CSS, and do not use wa-details or wa-accordion.

alternatives.when: Use a CollapsiblePanel for a rail or drawer that collapses beside the work area.

appOwns: the initial open state, and closing it from code (element.open = false)
reacting to the native toggle event (captured, through toggleAction)
variants: a quiet detail after the title
an exclusive accordion group sharing a name
accessibility: The native summary is a button that Enter and Space toggle and that reports its expanded state; the DisclosureArrow is decorative.
Keep the title a short, meaningful name for the hidden content; the open state survives re-renders because the platform owns it.

notes: The root takes the content-item geometry (8px inline margin, a 1px border, 8px padding); the content starts on the title's text column.

entries.name: Application Tabs
entries.description: Controlled document tabs with application-owned state and panels.
entries.purpose: Show TabBarItem and TabBar in a complete controlled composition.
useWhen: Compose application state, panels, actions, overflow, and reordering around TabBar and TabBarItem.
avoidWhen: Use SegmentedControl instead for a compact local choice.
accessibility: Keep one selected tab synchronized with one named tabpanel and retain the wireTabBars disposer.

entries.name: TabBarItem
entries.description: Roving-tabindex-ready tabs with typed compact, segmented, icon-only, drop-target, pinned, and name-overflow presentations.
entries.purpose: Render a controlled application tab with compact or icon-only presentation, a visible drop target, optional full-name display, and an optional pinned leading position.
useWhen: Render one controlled application tab inside TabBar.
avoidWhen: Do not render alone or use for a compact settings choice.
variants: label maximum width and ellipsis or visible name overflow
pinned leading position within a scrolling tablist
accessibility: Compose in a tablist and pair with an application-owned tabpanel.
Keep closeIcon decorative and free of interactive descendants; the owning close button supplies its accessible name and interaction.
Use rootAttributes only for application data-* metadata; component-owned identity, state, action, and role semantics are protected at runtime.

entries.name: TabBar
entries.description: Controlled tab strips with typed presentation and allocation, a scroll-owning tab region, an optional adjacent trailing action, and a separately pinned far-edge end action.
entries.purpose: Controlled tab strips whose tabs shrink and scroll while fixed leading, trailing, and far-edge end actions remain visible.
useWhen: Switch application tabpanels with optional overflow, closing, and reordering.
avoidWhen: Do not use for a compact local toggle or a long value list.
variants: standalone Web Awesome action in trailing or end
overflow dividers on each side with tabs scrolled out of view (wired by wireScrollDividers)
accessibility: Keep exactly one selected tab at tabindex 0 and preserve the wiring keyboard model.
Call wireTabBars for keyboard focus and selection, including the pinned leading tab's WebKit RTL scroll correction.

notes: TabBar owns inline flex allocation: tabs shrink and scroll, an adjacent trailing action follows the tab strip, and the end action stays pinned at the far edge; leading, trailing, and end actions do not shrink.

stateAttributes.name: data-tab-dragging
stateAttributes.meaning: "true" on the tab being dragged.

stateAttributes.name: data-tab-drop-position
stateAttributes.meaning: "before" or "after" on the tab under the pointer: where the dragged tab would land.

stateAttributes.name: data-tab-autoscroll
stateAttributes.meaning: "start" or "end" while a drag near that edge auto-scrolls the strip.

stateAttributes.name: data-scroll-overflow
stateAttributes.meaning: The physical edges, in canonical t/r/b/l order, beyond which content is scrolled out of view; absent when nothing is hidden (content that fits never reports its far edges). Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

stateAttributes.name: data-scroll-divider
stateAttributes.on: chrome named in wireScrollDividers targets (a TabBar strip has none)
stateAttributes.meaning: The sides, in t/r/b/l order, on which that chrome currently draws its scroll divider. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

stateAttributes.name: data-header-overlay
stateAttributes.meaning: measured once the wiring has measured a Pane's overlay header (headerPresentation: overlay) and published its border-box height as --kui-scroll-clearance-block-start on the Pane root, plus a classic content scrollbar's inline size as --kui-pane-scrollbar-inline-size, which the header leaves uncovered. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

entries.name: SegmentedControl
entries.description: Controlled exclusive choices in toolbar, rounded-rectangle, and pill presentations.
entries.purpose: Controlled exclusive choices in toolbar, rounded-rectangle, and pill presentations.
useWhen: Expose a small controlled exclusive choice set.
avoidWhen: Do not use for tabpanel semantics or many choices.
accessibility: Keep choice labels meaningful and every enabled native button in sequential Tab order.

entries.name: ChoiceChips
entries.description: A wrapping set of separated pill chips backed by native radios (one exclusive value) or, with multiple, native checkboxes (any number of values), with optional leading color swatches or icons.
entries.purpose: Choose one value, or with multiple any number of values, from a visible set too large for a segmented track, such as a color palette with labeled swatches or a set of annotation intents.
useWhen: Expose one exclusive choice among several visible options that must wrap onto more rows, such as a labeled color palette with swatches.
Set multiple when the person may turn any number of visible, wrapping options on or off, such as label filters or annotation intents.
avoidWhen: Use SegmentedControl for a few compact choices on one track.
Use Select when the choice list is long or space is tight; a multiple Select keeps a long multi-value list behind one trigger.
Do not use it for removable tags (Chip).

alternatives.when: Use ChoiceChips instead of button-appearance radios that must wrap; a joined button group wraps into ragged rows with shared borders.

variants: color swatch, transparent (struck-through) swatch, icon, or text-only choices
single (radios), multiple: 'toggle' (checkboxes), or multiple: true (a modifier-key multi-select listbox)
accessibility: The single group is a named role="radiogroup" of native radios: one Tab stop, arrow keys move the selection, and the checked radio submits the form value.

A multiple: 'toggle' group is a named role="group" of native checkboxes: each pill is a Tab stop, a click or Space toggles it alone, its checked state is native, and every checked value submits under name.

A multiple: true group is a named role="listbox" with aria-multiselectable whose chips are role="option" with aria-selected: one Tab stop (roving tabindex). A click selects one chip, Cmd on Apple platforms or Ctrl elsewhere toggles one, and Shift extends a range from the anchor; arrows, Home, and End move the selection, Shift with them extends it, Cmd/Ctrl with them moves focus alone, Space toggles, Shift+Space extends, and Cmd/Ctrl+A selects all. Hidden inputs submit every selected value under name, and wireChoiceChips fires change on the group.
Every choice keeps a visible text label; the swatch is decorative and the selection adds a heavier border, so neither relies on color alone.
Every color is a theme token, so a dark appearance scope (.wa-dark, .wa-invert, or any color-scheme: dark ancestor) restyles the chips for inverse chrome.

wiring.reason: Gives a multiple: true group its listbox selection: pointer and keyboard gestures, roving focus, aria-selected, hidden form inputs, and a change event on the group. Radio and toggle groups use native inputs and need no wiring.

entries.name: ColorSwatches
entries.description: A fixed palette: a native radio group of round color swatches with no visible text, each named by its color, the chosen one ringed independently of hue, with a struck-through no-color swatch, compact size, and disabled state.
entries.purpose: Let a person choose one color from a small fixed palette (a label, tag, or command color), or no color.
useWhen: A setting takes one color from a small, curated palette (a label, calendar, or command color): render ColorSwatches with name, a label, swatches, and value, and read the choice on change.
No color is a valid choice: include a swatch with color 'transparent'.
avoidWhen: Do not use it when any color is allowed; use a ColorPicker or ColorField.
Do not use it for choices that are not colors; use ChoiceChips or a RadioGroup.
Do not put text in the swatches; the color's label names each one.

alternatives.when: Use ChoiceChips with swatches when each color also needs a visible name.
Use a RadioGroup for choices that are not colors.

appOwns: the palette and its color names
the chosen value (read it on change through action)
the field name and form association
variants: fixed palette with a visible label
accessibility: It is a native radio group: Tab reaches it once and the arrow keys move the choice; each radio is named by its color label, also shown as the swatch's hover hint.
The chosen swatch wears a ring in the text color set off by a gap, so the choice never depends on hue; forced colors draw it in Highlight.

notes: The group takes the shared block-content inset (a transparent 1px border and 8px padding), so its label sits on the text column; each swatch keeps 4px of room for its ring, pulled back at the row's edges.

entries.name: ColorPicker
entries.description: A full inline color picker: a saturation and brightness area, hue and opacity sliders, an RGB/HSL/HSB/Grayscale model menu with channel fields, a hex field (8 digits below full opacity) and opacity field, a screen sampler where the EyeDropper API exists, and optional preset and sample swatches.
entries.purpose: Let a person choose any color precisely, by dragging, typing channel or hex values, sampling the screen, or picking a preset or saved sample.
useWhen: Any color is allowed and the person may need precision (a fill, stroke, or brand color): render ColorPicker with value, wire wireColorPickers with onChange, and re-render with the reported value and mode.
A design tool keeps presets or saved colors: pass presets, samples, and addSampleAction.
avoidWhen: Do not use it for a small curated palette; use ColorSwatches.
Do not leave it always open in a form; use ColorField, which opens it from a swatch and hex trigger.
Do not use wa-color-picker or a native color input styled by hand.

alternatives.when: Use ColorSwatches for a fixed palette.

appOwns: the value and mode (update them from onChange and re-render)
presets and samples, and adding to samples on addSampleAction
the field name and form association
variants: RGB, HSL, HSB, or Grayscale channel fields
presets and titled sample groups with an add button
screen sampler where the EyeDropper API exists
accessibility: The area is a slider named Saturation and Brightness with a spoken value; the arrow keys move it (Shift for 10% steps), Page Up and Down change brightness, Home and End saturation.
Hue and opacity are native range inputs; every field is named (Red, Hue, Hex Color, Opacity); the picker is a named group.

notes: The panel takes the shared block-content inset and a 320px maximum width; its rows are 12px apart.

stateAttributes.name: data-shown
stateAttributes.meaning: The text a channel, hex, or opacity field last showed, so leaving an unedited field commits nothing.

stateAttributes.name: data-count
stateAttributes.meaning: How many channel fields the current model shows (1 for Grayscale, 3 otherwise).

entries.name: ColorField
entries.description: A form field for a color: a label above a trigger that shows the color as a swatch (over a checkerboard) and its hex value, opening a ColorPicker in an AnchoredSurface below it, with a hint or error, compact size, required, disabled, and a hidden input for the hex value.
entries.purpose: Put a color choice in a form or inspector without keeping a full picker open.
useWhen: A form or inspector row sets one color (a fill, border, or theme color): render ColorField with id, label, value, and mode, wire wireColorFields with onChange, and re-render with the reported value and mode.
The popup picker should offer presets or samples: pass them through wireColorFields' pickers option, keyed by field id.
avoidWhen: Do not use it when the color is the main task of the view; show a ColorPicker inline.
Do not use it for a small curated palette; use ColorSwatches.
Do not use wa-color-picker.

alternatives.when: Use an inline ColorPicker when choosing the color is the view's main task.
Use ColorSwatches for a fixed palette.

appOwns: the value and model (update them from onChange and re-render)
per-field picker presets and samples (wireColorFields pickers)
the field name and form association
accessibility: The trigger is a button named by the label and the current hex value, with aria-haspopup dialog and aria-expanded; the hint and error describe it.
The picker opens in a non-modal AnchoredSurface named by the label; Escape or a press outside closes it and focus returns to the trigger.

notes: The trigger matches TextField's box, label, hint, and error geometry.

stateAttributes.name: data-value
stateAttributes.meaning: The committed color, updated by the wiring until the app re-renders, so reopening the picker starts from the last edit.

stateAttributes.name: data-mode
stateAttributes.meaning: The committed color model, updated the same way as data-value.

entries.name: MessageComposer
entries.description: A raised chat or prompt composer: a framed message field that grows with its content above a compact Toolbar action row with leading controls, a hint, and a send button.
entries.purpose: Write a chat message or prompt in a raised frame whose border turns brand while focus is within, with a field that grows between row bounds and a trailing send action.
useWhen: Write a chat message, assistant prompt, or comment reply that is sent with a trailing action, especially in a DialogSurface floating footer over a transcript.
avoidWhen: Use wa-textarea with a FieldLabel for an ordinary form field that is submitted with the rest of a form.
Do not wrap it in another framed ContentItem or card; it owns its frame, padding, and shadow.

alternatives.when: Use MessageComposer instead of a wa-textarea and a button in app-styled chrome for a chat or prompt composer; it owns the raised frame, focus-within border, auto-grow, and action row.

appOwns: keyboard shortcuts other than the opt-in Enter-to-send
disabled and busy state of its actions
variants: minRows and maxRows bounds for the growing field
optional hint, described by the field when an id is given
optional leading controls (attach, model Select) in the Toolbar action row's leading zone
submitOnEnter: Enter or Cmd/Ctrl+Enter activates the first trailing action, Shift+Enter inserts a newline (with wireMessageComposers)
slotted into a DialogSurface floating footer
accessibility: The field is a native textarea named by label; with an id, the hint is its accessible description.
The frame's brand border shows focus within; the action row is a compact Toolbar footer named "<label> Actions", and its controls keep their own names and focus rings.
With submitOnEnter the field announces aria-keyshortcuts="Enter"; Shift+Enter keeps a newline, and an Enter that commits an IME composition never sends.

wiring.reason: Only for submitOnEnter: turns Enter (or Cmd/Ctrl+Enter) in the field into a click on the first trailing action, skipping Shift+Enter, IME composition, empty or whitespace-only messages, auto-repeat, and a disabled or loading action.

entries.name: SearchField
entries.description: Token-controlled, optionally collapsible search editor with ordered, editable, removable filter chips.
entries.purpose: Token-controlled, optionally collapsible search editor with ordered, editable, removable filter chips.
useWhen: Combine DOM-owned free text with ordered editable/removable filter tokens in one searchbox.
Enable collapsible mode when an empty, unfocused search should reduce to one iconic action, standalone or inside a toolbar group.
Use presentation="form-field" for a structured search query beside Web Awesome form controls, with a visible label, optional hint, and required marker.
avoidWhen: Do not use for ordinary text input or separately labeled filter controls.
appOwns: the grammar and evaluation callback when using the optional managed model, or parsing, suggestions, tokens, and query execution in manual mode

reading the managed model without subscribing per keystroke: SearchField subscribes only to model.structure (committed tokens, empty or non-empty text, editor revision) and model.suggestions, so plain typing never re-runs the host render; in the host's own render, read model.state.peek() or bind model.result (or a computed) as a fine-grained signal hole instead of reading model.state.value
the revision that rebuilds the DOM-owned editor for a programmatic text replacement
optional override of the collapsible expand/collapse/focus, which wireSearchFields manages by default (adopt an app expanded signal, opt out per behavior, or drive it via the returned handle)
validation of a required form-field value
variants: visible form-field label, hint, and required marker
accessibility: Announce result changes when useful and keep tokens atomic during editing.

Keep leading and trailing controls aligned to the first text line while content wraps. Managed Clear restores replacement focus before the next input task, preserving immediate typing and later focus handoffs without a frame delay.

Wire Enter to submit without inserting a contenteditable line break and preserve focus plus the text-relative caret across controlled keyboard chip deletion before the next keystroke. Select All deletion preserves managed open state and replacement focus; persist both edited query and tokens. Visual wrapping remains available.

In collapsible mode, wireSearchFields manages this by default: activating the trigger reveals the searchbox and moves focus into it, Escape on an empty field collapses and returns focus to the trigger, and focus leaving an empty field collapses it; each behavior is individually opt-out.

The form-field presentation associates its visible label and optional hint with the searchbox, exposes aria-required when required, and lets wireSearchFields focus the editor from a label click. The app validates required input.

stateAttributes.name: data-search-field-text
stateAttributes.meaning: Marks the plain-text span the helper inserts when the editor is emptied.

stateAttributes.name: data-empty
stateAttributes.meaning: "true" on that span while it holds no text.

stateAttributes.name: data-placeholder-visible
stateAttributes.meaning: Tracks whether the DOM-owned editor is empty so its placeholder stays outside the editable area.

entries.name: TagField
entries.description: A form field that collects short values as removable tags: SearchField's token editor in its form-field presentation, with a label, hint or error, a leading tag glyph, chips that edit or remove, a clear button, an optional max, and a hidden input per tag submitted under its name.
entries.purpose: Collect a list of short values (labels, recipients, keywords) as removable tags, each submitted as its own form value.
useWhen: A form collects several short values of one kind (labels, recipients, keywords): render TagField with tags and name, wire wireTagFields with onChange, and re-render with the list it reports.
Values must be checked (an email shape, a known label) or capped: pass normalize and max, and show onReject's reason as the field's error.
avoidWhen: Do not use it for search filters; SearchField combines free text with ordered, editable filter tokens.
Do not use it to pick from a short fixed set; use ChoiceChips or a multiple Select.
Do not use wa-tag-input.

alternatives.when: Use SearchField when the tokens are search filters rather than submitted form values.
Use ChoiceChips to pick several from a short known set.

appOwns: the tag list (update it from onChange and re-render)
validation and normalization (normalize) and showing refusals (onReject, error)
the field name and form association
variants: validated with max and an error
custom delimiters and duplicate policy (wireTagFields options)
accessibility: The editor is named by the visible label and described by the hint or error; each chip has an edit button (its label) and a remove button named for the tag.

Enter or a delimiter adds the typed text, Backspace at the start removes the last tag, ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move between chips and the editor, and Backspace or Delete on a focused chip removes it.

notes: The SearchField form-field presentation draws the label, frame, chips, and hint; TagField adds no geometry of its own.

entries.name: ResizableRegion
entries.description: Pointer and keyboard-operable split region with a customizable handle icon.
entries.purpose: Pointer and keyboard-operable split region with a customizable handle icon.
useWhen: Provide a controlled user-resizable application pane.
avoidWhen: Do not use for static columns; use CSS grid.
variants: inline, overlay, or hidden responsive presentation
accessibility: Preserve separator naming, value ARIA, and keyboard behavior.
Keep handleIcon decorative and free of interactive descendants; the separator owns focus, naming, and pointer/keyboard interaction.

notes: The region delegates visible separator geometry and hit-area padding to its orientation-specific handle.

stateAttributes.name: data-handle-inset
stateAttributes.meaning: Present while a clipping edge clamps the region: the handle and its focus ring sit inside the region instead of overhanging that edge.

stateAttributes.name: data-resizing
stateAttributes.meaning: "true" during an active pointer drag of the handle.

entries.name: Select
entries.description: Controlled Kerf select with typed single or multiple values, disabled choices, optional bulk actions, and form, toolbar, navigation, compact, icon-only, truncating, hint, and grouped-choice presentations; a native trigger and a top-layer listbox wired by select/register.
entries.purpose: Choose one or more controlled values, keep unavailable choices visible, and optionally select all enabled choices or clear a multiple selection.
useWhen: Choose a controlled value from a moderate or long list, including grouped and icon-bearing choices.

Color an optional choice icon with a CssForegroundColor: uiColor() with a foreground token such as success-on-quiet, foregroundColorVar() for an app-owned property, or foregroundColor() for a direct custom CSS color. Fill tokens such as success are backgrounds that leave the icon nearly invisible, so they, lengths, raw color strings, and unqualified colorVar() values are rejected.
Use the default content-sized menu for long option labels; native popup shifting keeps it within 10px viewport gutters. fitMenu instead matches trigger width and wraps labels.
avoidWhen: Do not use for commands or a small choice set that should stay visible.

alternatives.when: Use Combobox when people may type to filter or create a new value.

variants: fit-content, max-content, or fill trigger width
custom selected content typography and ellipsis
disabled choice with an optional reason
opt-in select-all and clear actions for multiple selection
multiple icon-only filter trigger with a fixed triggerIcon
maxTriggerWidth / minTriggerWidth bounds on the closed trigger under any presentation, ellipsizing custom selected content
accessibility: Verify the live value, standard events, focus, and rendered output.

The trigger is a native button with role="combobox", aria-haspopup="listbox", and aria-expanded. A nonempty label names it (the visible label is aria-hidden text beside it); otherwise ariaLabel names it without adding control height, including custom selected content.
Hint text is visible below the control and is the trigger's aria-description; placeholderText remains the empty value inside the closed control.

Import select/register once: it defines the form-associated kui-select root (value, name, form submission, and form reset) and wires every Select in the document. The listbox opens below the trigger in the top layer, flipping above when short and capped at the viewport edges. Do not add consumer popup timing or position repairs.

Keyboard: Enter, Space, ArrowDown, or ArrowUp on the trigger opens on the chosen option (Home/End on the first/last), and typing opens on a matching label; in the listbox the arrows move and wrap, Home/End jump, typing a label's first letters moves to it, Enter or Space chooses, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger, and Tab closes and continues from the trigger.

With multiple, the listbox (aria-multiselectable) stays open while choices toggle (pointer, Enter, or Space) and closes on an outside press, Escape, or Tab; each chosen option shows a check, and the closed control summarizes the chosen labels in choice order.

Disabled choices stay visible with aria-disabled but cannot be chosen; disabledReason is their title. A multiple Select can opt in to localized select-all and clear buttons below the listbox, which skip disabled choices and publish ordinary change events for changed values.

A multiple icon-only trigger shows its fixed triggerIcon and, while any choice is chosen, an aria-hidden count Badge; the trigger's accessible name ends with the chosen labels in choice order, and its value text stays empty.

Once registered, an icon-only trigger (single or multiple) shows an aria-hidden help tag repeating its accessible name (a single Select adds its current choice) after a 500ms hover and at once on keyboard focus; it hides while the listbox is open, on a press, and on Escape, and never joins aria-labelledby. Do not add a title or another tooltip.

entries.name: Combobox
entries.description: A free-text field with a filtered suggestion list that can also create a new value.
entries.purpose: Let people pick an existing value or create a new one by typing (tags, labels, recipients), with the themed field chrome, the ARIA combobox pattern, and a touch-safe font size, without a native datalist or app CSS.
useWhen: People type to find an existing value among many, or create a new one (tags, labels, recipients).
avoidWhen: Do not use when only existing values are allowed and nothing needs typing; use Select.
Do not use for free text plus removable filter tokens in one editor; use SearchField.
Do not style a native input with a datalist from app CSS.

alternatives.when: Use Select when only existing values are allowed.
Use SearchField for search text with removable filter tokens.

appOwns: the suggestions and the committed values
clearing the field after a commit
accessibility: Native input with role=combobox, aria-autocomplete=list, aria-expanded, aria-controls, and aria-activedescendant; options are role=option in a listbox. The visible label is a real label; the hint is aria-describedby.

notes: Label and hint sit on the value's text column (1px border + 8px padding); the 44px field matches a themed wa-input.

wiring.reason: Filters suggestions, moves the active option, and reports commits; without it the list never opens.

stateAttributes.name: data-value
stateAttributes.meaning: The typed text the create option would commit; rewritten as the person types.

entries.name: TextField
entries.description: A labeled single-line input or multi-line textarea with hint and error text, an optional leading icon, clear button, and character count, at the 44px control height or compact.
entries.purpose: Collect free text (names, addresses, notes, comments) with Kerf's field chrome, a visible or accessible label, supporting and validation text, and native input semantics.
useWhen: A form or dialog collects a line of free text: label names it (or ariaLabel when nearby content already does), hint explains it, and error reports a validation problem.
People write a longer note or message: multiline with rows, or rows plus maxRows to grow with the content; maxLength with showCount shows the remaining budget.
A filter or search field needs a leading icon and a clear button: icon and clearable.
avoidWhen: Do not use when only existing values are allowed; use Select.
Do not use when people pick among suggestions or create tags; use Combobox.
Do not use for search text with removable filter tokens; use SearchField.
Do not use for a chat-style message with a send action; use MessageComposer.

alternatives.when: Use Combobox when people pick among suggestions or create a value.
Use MessageComposer for a message with a send action.

variants: multiline (fixed rows or growing to maxRows)
email, password, search, url, tel, or number type
accessibility: The whole field is a <label> around a native <input> or <textarea>, so clicking anywhere on it focuses the field; the input is named by label (aria-label, with the visible label text hidden from assistive technology so the clear button and count stay out of the name) or by ariaLabel. Focus shows the standard focus ring around the box.

The hint and error are visible below the field and form the input's aria-description; an error also sets aria-invalid="true". The clear button is a native button named by clearLabel (default Clear), hidden while the field is empty, and returns focus to the field.
Compact text grows to 16px on coarse-pointer touch screens so iOS does not zoom on focus.

notes: Label, hint, and error sit on the value's text column (1px border + 8px padding); the 44px box matches Button and Select, and compact matches their compact 33px.

wiring.reason: Makes clearable fields clear themselves (announcing input and change) and keeps showCount counts current; a field without either works without it.

entries.name: Checkbox
entries.description: A native checkbox drawn as a Kerf box beside its label, with hint and error text on the label's column, a mixed (indeterminate) state, and native form participation.
entries.purpose: Turn one independent option on or off in a form or settings list, including a parent whose children are partly checked, without Web Awesome.
useWhen: A form or settings list has an independent yes/no option that is submitted or applied with the rest of the form.
A parent option summarizes partly checked children: indeterminate, with wireCheckboxes(root).
avoidWhen: Do not use for a setting that applies the moment it changes; use Switch.
Do not use for one choice among several; use RadioGroup, ChoiceChips, or SegmentedControl.
Do not use for several wrapping tag-like choices; use ChoiceChips multiple.

alternatives.when: Use Switch for a setting that applies immediately.
Use ChoiceChips multiple for several visible, wrapping choices.

accessibility: A native <input type="checkbox"> inside its <label>, invisibly over the drawn box, so the label names it and pointer, keyboard, touch exploration, and forms reach the real control; Space toggles it and focus shows the focus ring on the box.

The hint and error form the input's aria-description; an error sets aria-invalid="true" and the danger border. indeterminate sets the native indeterminate property through wireCheckboxes, so assistive technology reports a mixed state.

notes: A 20px box (18px compact) 8px (7px) before its label; hint and error align with the label text.

wiring.reason: Sets the native indeterminate property, which only script can set, from the rendered marker; a Checkbox without indeterminate works without it.

entries.name: RadioGroup
entries.description: A native fieldset of radios, each drawn as a Kerf circle beside its label, with the group label above, per-choice hints, and hint and error text below, stacked or wrapping.
entries.purpose: Choose exactly one of a few options that should stay visible with room for a label and hint each, with native keyboard behavior and form participation.
useWhen: A form asks for one of two to about six options that people should compare at a glance, each with a readable label and an optional hint.
avoidWhen: Do not use for many options or a compact toolbar value; use Select.
Do not use to switch a view; use SegmentedControl.
Do not use for chip-styled or color choices; use ChoiceChips.

alternatives.when: Use Select for a long list.
Use ChoiceChips for wrapping pill choices.

accessibility: A native <fieldset role="radiogroup"> named by its legend (label) or ariaLabel; each choice is a native radio inside its <label>, invisibly over the drawn circle. The browser owns the interaction: one Tab stop, arrow keys move and select, and the checked radio submits its value under name.

The group's hint and error form its aria-description; an error sets aria-invalid on the group and the danger border on each circle. required sets each radio's native required and aria-required on the group. A choice's hint is that radio's aria-description.

notes: The label and hint sit on the text column (1px + 8px); the choices sit on the 8px control column, 12px apart.

entries.name: Switch
entries.description: An on/off setting that applies immediately: a native checkbox with role="switch" drawn as a track and thumb beside its label, with a hint on the label's column.
entries.purpose: Turn a setting on or off the moment it changes, such as live updates or a preference, without Web Awesome.
useWhen: A setting takes effect immediately when toggled, in a settings list or a pane footer.
avoidWhen: Do not use for an option a form submits later; use Checkbox.
Do not use for an icon-only toolbar toggle; use an icon-only Button with pressed, or a ToolbarControlGroup toggle.

alternatives.when: Use Checkbox for an option a form submits.
Use an icon-only Button with pressed for an icon-only toggle.

accessibility: A native <input type="checkbox" role="switch"> inside its <label>, invisibly over the drawn track, so the label names it and assistive technology announces on or off; Space toggles it and focus shows the focus ring on the track. The hint is its aria-description. The thumb's slide is skipped when reduced motion is preferred.

notes: A 35×20 track (31.5×18 compact) 8px (7px) before its label; the hint aligns with the label text.

entries.name: Slider
entries.description: A value on a continuous or stepped range: a native range input drawn as a track, a brand fill, and a thumb, with a label row, an optional live readout and unit, labeled tick stops, a hint, compact size, and disabled state.
entries.purpose: Let a person pick a value from a range where the relative position matters more than an exact number (volume, zoom, opacity, a threshold).
useWhen: A setting is a value in a known range and dragging to it is natural (volume, zoom, opacity): render Slider with min, max, step, and a label; add showValue and unit for a readout.
Discrete stops deserve names under the track: pass ticks.
avoidWhen: Do not use it when the exact number matters or the range is huge; use a TextField with type number.
Do not use it for an on/off choice (use Switch) or for a few named options (use SegmentedControl).
Do not use wa-slider.

alternatives.when: Use a SegmentedControl for a handful of named options.
Use a numeric TextField when the exact value matters.

appOwns: the value (read it on input or change through action) and re-rendering with it
variants: labeled with a live readout and unit
accessibility: It is a native range input: arrow keys, Page Up and Down, Home, and End step it, and the platform announces its value (with a unit, as aria-valuetext).
The label names it, the hint describes it, and the readout is hidden from assistive technology because the input already reports its value; forced colors draw a Highlight fill on a GrayText track.

notes: It fills the available width with the shared block-content inset (a transparent 1px border and 8px padding), so its label sits on the text column.

entries.name: AnchoredSurface
entries.description: A styled non-modal surface for app-owned interactive help or popup content, anchored to an element or pointer.
entries.purpose: Present arbitrary app-owned content next to an element or pointer with Kerf UI surface styling and kerfjs/overlay lifecycle.
useWhen: Show interactive help or other arbitrary content near a control or pointer, including inside a modal dialog.
avoidWhen: Use PopupMenu for a typed action menu, Select for a choice, and a modal dialog for a task that must block the page.
appOwns: opening trigger and programmatic close after an action
variants: tone: 'dark' (the inverse tone of a dark ToolbarControlGroup, for popups anchored to media chrome)

usageExamples.title: Interactive help
usageExamples.description: The trigger owns when to open; the returned handle closes when an action completes.
usageExamples.code:
const handle = openAnchoredSurface(button, () => <HelpPanel />, { label: 'Field help' });
// Close from the app's action handler: handle.close();

usageExamples.title: Popup anchored to dark media chrome
usageExamples.description: tone: 'dark' matches a ToolbarControlGroup tone="dark": the surface takes the opposite of the anchor's color scheme (openAnchoredSurfaceAt reads it from point.context) and follows a live OS-preference or ancestor theme switch while open, so its content inherits the inverse text, border, and focus colors without overrides.

accessibility: The non-modal surface has role dialog and the required label. Focus moves to the first focusable descendant by default and returns to the opener on close; initialFocus: false leaves focus on the trigger. Escape and outside press dismiss by default.

entries.name: PopupMenu
entries.description: A typed action menu with nested choices, selected state, and optional pointer-anchored context opening, drawn by Kerf as a native menu in the top layer.
entries.purpose: A typed action menu with nested choices, selected state, and optional pointer-anchored context opening, drawn by Kerf as a native menu in the top layer.
useWhen: Offer a short list of commands behind one trigger, such as a toolbar sort or More menu.
Group related commands under headings and dividers in one popup.
Nest decisions under a parent command, show checked or trailing choice state, or open a context menu at pointer coordinates.
avoidWhen: Do not use it to choose a persistent value (use Select) or for navigation rows (use ListItem).
Do not hand-write wa-dropdown / wa-dropdown-item markup for an action menu; use PopupMenu.
appOwns: the checked state of checkbox choices, which the menu reports as requested in its kui-menu-select event
reactions to the menu opening or closing
contextmenu event handling and identification of the menu root when using a pointer-anchored context menu
variants: context trigger with a rendered anchor point and a zero-footprint anchor host

usageExamples.title: Nested decisions
usageExamples.description: The app owns the current decision, batch disabled state, and delegated actions. Each child keeps its own record metadata.
usageExamples.code:
<PopupMenu
  label="Line actions"
  items={[
    { label: 'Decide', submenu: [
      { label: 'Approve', action: 'decide', checked: current === 'approve',
        attributes: { 'data-line-id': lineId, 'data-decision': 'approve' } },
      { label: 'Reject', action: 'decide', tone: 'danger',
        disabled: needsPrice, disabledReason: needsPrice ? 'Add a price first' : undefined,
        attributes: { 'data-line-id': lineId, 'data-decision': 'reject' } },
    ] },
    { kind: 'divider' },
    { label: 'Remove', action: 'remove', tone: 'danger' },
  ]}
/>

usageExamples.title: Flat selected choices
usageExamples.description: Headings separate sort dimensions; trailing safe content marks the active command without changing its accessible label.
usageExamples.code:
<PopupMenu
  label="Sort chat"
  items={[
    { kind: 'heading', label: 'Sort By' },
    { label: 'Updated', action: 'sort-updated', details: sort === 'updated' ? tick : undefined },
    { label: 'Priority', action: 'sort-priority', details: sort === 'priority' ? tick : undefined },
    { kind: 'heading', label: 'Order' },
    { label: 'Newest First', action: 'order-newest', details: order === 'newest' ? tick : undefined },
  ]}
/>

usageExamples.title: Pointer anchored context menu
usageExamples.description: Keep the row's visible disabled action separate from the context menu anchor. Find the menu root with a stable data attribute.
usageExamples.code:
<PopupMenu
  context
  label="Demand Actions"
  rootAttributes={{ 'data-demand-menu': '' }}
  items={[{ label: 'Open', action: 'open-demand' }]}
/>
// In the app's row wiring:
row.addEventListener('contextmenu', (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  const menu = row.querySelector('[data-demand-menu]') as PopupMenuElement;
  openPopupMenuAt(menu, event.clientX, event.clientY);
});
// Call closePopupMenu(menu) when the app needs to dismiss it.

accessibility: The trigger is a native button with aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded; an icon-only trigger requires label, rendered as visually hidden text inside the button, and a trigger with visible text is named by that text. The context anchor stays out of the accessibility tree. The open menu (role="menu") takes the trigger's name, each submenu takes its parent item's label, and a heading names the role="group" that holds its items, so a screen reader announces named menus and getByRole('menu', { name }) finds them. Items are menuitem or menuitemcheckbox buttons with aria-checked and aria-disabled.

Keyboard: Enter, Space, or ArrowDown on the trigger opens on the first item (ArrowUp on the last); ArrowUp/ArrowDown move and wrap past disabled items, Home/End jump, and typing a label's first letters moves to it; Enter or Space chooses; ArrowRight opens a submenu on its first item and ArrowLeft returns to the parent item (mirrored right to left); Escape closes the current level and returns focus to its opener; Tab closes the menu and continues from the trigger.

Once registered, an icon-only trigger shows its label as an aria-hidden help tag after a 500ms hover and at once on keyboard focus; it hides while the menu is open, on a press, and on Escape, and never joins aria-labelledby. Do not add a title or another tooltip.

entries.name: Button
entries.description: A standalone action button: a native button (or a link with href) in a neutral, brand, or danger tone and a primary, secondary, or plain emphasis, at the 44px control height or compact.
entries.purpose: Trigger an action from a dialog footer, a form, or content outside any Toolbar, with Kerf's button chrome and native button semantics.
useWhen: A dialog footer, a form, or content needs an action button: tone="brand" for the main action, tone="danger" for a destructive one, and emphasis="secondary" or "plain" for the quieter actions beside it.
A form submits or resets: type="submit" or "reset" (the default type never submits), with name, value, and form when needed.
An action navigates: href renders a link with the same chrome.
avoidWhen: Do not use inside a ToolbarControlGroup; give the group plain <button> controls, which it styles.
Do not use for an icon-only action; use an icon-only Button (with pressed for an on/off toggle).
Do not use for a menu trigger; use PopupMenu.

alternatives.when: Inside a Toolbar, compose plain buttons in a ToolbarControlGroup.

appOwns: the label and its delegated action
what a press does while loading
variants: icon-only square (icon and ariaLabel, no label)
pressed toggle (aria-pressed) on any tone and emphasis
accessibility: A native <button> (type="button" unless set) or, with href, an <a>; its label names it, or ariaLabel when the label is not enough. Focus shows the standard focus ring.
Loading shows a spinner in place of the label, which still names the button, and sets aria-busy="true". A disabled link drops its href and reports aria-disabled="true".

With pressed, it is a toggle: aria-pressed reports the state, and the pressed look adds a doubled outline (secondary and plain) or a darkened fill with an inset ring (primary), so the state never relies on hue alone; forced-colors mode paints it Highlight. An icon-only Button is named by ariaLabel, and help tags show that name on hover and keyboard focus. A title gives native hover text that says more than the name and replaces the help tag.

entries.name: SplitButton
entries.description: A primary action with an attached options trigger on one loud semantic fill.
entries.purpose: Render a prominent primary action plus an options trigger (provider, model, target) as one control with a semantic tone, full-width sizing, a busy presentation, and native aria-expanded on the trigger, outside any Toolbar.
useWhen: A prominent primary action has a closely related set of options chosen from an attached trigger, such as Drive with a provider menu or Deploy with targets.
avoidWhen: Do not use for a plain action without options; use wa-button.
Do not use inside a Toolbar for a command menu; use PopupMenu in a ToolbarControlGroup.
Do not use wa-button-group to build one; its hosts do not forward aria-expanded or names to their inner buttons.

alternatives.when: SplitButton's native halves expose names and aria-expanded directly.
Open the app's options menu from optionsAction; PopupMenu remains the command menu inside a toolbar.

appOwns: the options menu and its open state
the running state, tone switch, and copy
variants: brand, neutral, success, warning, or danger tone
accessibility: Both halves are native buttons in a group; the options trigger exposes aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, and optional aria-controls, and needs optionsLabel. busy sets aria-busy on the primary.

entries.name: FilePicker
entries.description: A compact browse trigger and a dashed drop zone around native file inputs, with wiring that reports chosen and dropped files.
entries.purpose: Let people choose or drop files (attachments, evidence, imports) without app CSS: a link-toned browse trigger and a dashed drop target that highlights while dragging, both around visually hidden native file inputs.
useWhen: People attach or import files by browsing or by dropping them onto a target.
avoidWhen: Do not style a native file input or label from app CSS; use these components.
Do not rely on the drop zone alone; it also opens the chooser when clicked or activated from the keyboard.

alternatives.when: A button cannot open the native chooser without script; the trigger is a label around the input.

appOwns: what happens to the reported files (upload, validation, limits)
accessibility: Each control is a label around a real file input that receives keyboard focus; the visible control shows the focus ring. Give the input an accessibleLabel when the visible copy is short.

notes: The drop zone carries the 8px content-item inline margin; the trigger is a compact 32px inline control.

wiring.reason: Reports chosen and dropped files and accepts drops on the zone; without it drops open the file in the browser.

stateAttributes.name: data-dragging
stateAttributes.meaning: "true" while files are dragged over the zone.

entries.name: Feedback
entries.description: Banners, empty states, and labeled progress.
entries.purpose: Banners, empty states, and labeled progress.
useWhen: Compose persistent status, empty/busy content, and compact loading feedback.
avoidWhen: Do not collapse different message lifetimes or urgency into one visual treatment.
accessibility: Choose polite status versus assertive alert deliberately.

entries.name: StateBanner
entries.description: Polite status and assertive alert feedback with semantic tones, plus non-status pop emphasis for featured or novel content.
entries.purpose: Present persistent inline feedback or attractive non-status emphasis with a named semantic tone.
useWhen: Place persistent inline semantic status beside affected work.
avoidWhen: Do not use for an absent-content screen or transient confirmation.
Do not use pop as a substitute for success, warning, or danger.

alternatives.when: Host app-level progress in a viewport corner with CornerStatus instead of fixed-position CSS.

accessibility: Use alert urgency only for an attention-requiring failure.
Keep optional badge content terse and do not rely on its tone alone for meaning.

entries.name: Toast
entries.description: Styling for kerfjs/overlay's toast(): a bottom-edge region of stacked, auto-dismissing notifications on the raised surface, with info, success, and warning tones, StateBanner content, and enter and exit motion.
entries.purpose: Show a brief, non-blocking confirmation or status message that dismisses itself, without hand-written toast CSS.
useWhen: A completed action needs brief, non-blocking confirmation (saved, copied, published): import @kerfjs/ui/overlay-toast.css once and call toast() from kerfjs/overlay with exitClass 'kui-toast-exit' and exitDuration 200.
A status message needs a tone or an icon and detail: pass variant ('info', 'success', 'warning') for a plain message, or render a StateBanner as the toast's only content.
A rapid sequence (repeated copy actions) should collapse to the latest message: mode 'replace'.
avoidWhen: Do not use a toast for an error the person must act on or a decision; use a StateBanner in the affected surface, or a DialogSurface.
Do not put controls that must stay reachable in a toast that dismisses itself; set duration 0 and dismiss it from your own action, or use a StateBanner.
Do not hand-write toast placement, stacking, or motion CSS, and do not use wa-toast.

alternatives.when: Use a StateBanner in place for a persistent status or an error tied to one surface.

appOwns: when to show a toast and its message
an app-owned container with data-placement="top" for top-edge stacking
variants: plain message on the raised surface
StateBanner as the toast's only content, taking the banner's tone and chrome
replace mode collapsing a rapid sequence to the latest
bottom-edge region by default, or top-edge stacking on an app-owned container with data-placement="top"
accessibility: The core region is an aria-live polite region and each toast is role status, so assistive technology announces it without moving focus.
Toasts dismiss themselves after four seconds by default; give longer messages a longer duration, and never rely on a toast for the only path to an action.
The entrance and exit only fade under prefers-reduced-motion or the static-effects switch, and forced colors draw a CanvasText border on Canvas.

notes: The region insets 16px from the viewport edge plus the safe area and caps its width at 480px; toasts stack with an 8px gap.

entries.name: Tooltip
entries.description: Styling for kerfjs/overlay's tooltip(): the help tag's look (loud neutral fill, on-loud 14px text, 3px radius) for a hover and focus tooltip on any element, wrapping at 40 characters, with entrance and exit motion.
entries.purpose: Explain a control or value on hover and keyboard focus with a styled tooltip, without hand-written tooltip CSS.
useWhen: A control or value needs a short explanation on hover and keyboard focus (a longer action description, a chart point, a truncated label): import @kerfjs/ui/overlay-tooltip.css once and call tooltip(anchor, content) from kerfjs/overlay with exitClass 'kui-tooltip-exit' and exitDuration 100.
The explanation has structure (a bold line over a detail): pass a render function; its content inherits the tooltip's colors.
avoidWhen: Do not add a tooltip to an icon-only control in a ToolbarControlGroup, an icon-only Button, Select, or PopupMenu; @kerfjs/ui/help-tags-register already shows its help tag.
Do not put interactive content or the only copy of important information in a tooltip; use an AnchoredSurface or visible text.
Do not hand-write tooltip CSS or use wa-tooltip.

alternatives.when: Use an AnchoredSurface for interactive or persistent help that the person opens.

appOwns: which elements get a tooltip and its content
placement, delay, and native top-layer hosting
the disposer that removes a tooltip's listeners
variants: plain text tooltip, wrapped at 40 characters
structured content from a render function
any placement tooltip() supports (top by default)
accessibility: tooltip() shows on hover and on keyboard focus, gives the wrapper role tooltip, and hides on leave or blur; keep the anchor's accessible name complete without it.
The loud neutral fill with on-loud text meets WCAG AA; forced colors draw CanvasText on Canvas, and the entrance is skipped under prefers-reduced-motion or the static-effects switch.

notes: tooltip() positions the wrapper beside its anchor; the stylesheet caps its width at 40 characters within the viewport.

entries.name: CornerStatus
entries.description: Non-dismissible app-level status pinned to a viewport corner in the top layer, hosting StateBanner.
entries.purpose: Show ongoing app-level progress such as "Loading…" or "Updating Tickets… 3 of 12" in a viewport corner above page chrome and any dialog opened before it, without a close button, light dismiss, Escape, or focus change.
useWhen: Show ongoing app-level progress or status that has no better home beside the affected work and must stay visible until the work ends.
avoidWhen: Do not use for transient, dismissible confirmation; use a toast.
Do not use for status that belongs beside the affected work; place a StateBanner there.
Do not position a StateBanner with fixed-position application CSS; use CornerStatus.

alternatives.when: Compose one or more StateBanners (urgency="status") inside it; they stack.
A toast item is transient and always dismissible; CornerStatus stays until the application removes it.

appOwns: status lifetime (render while the work runs, remove when it ends)
the composed StateBanner copy and progress
accessibility: The host adds no role; the composed StateBanner with urgency="status" is the polite live region.
Opening never moves focus, and there is no close button, light dismiss, or Escape handling to compete with dialogs.
A modal dialog opened while it shows stacks above it and makes it inert (unannounced); show progress the dialog's task depends on inside the dialog.

notes: Placement owns the 16px viewport gutter plus device safe-area insets; a StateBanner inside drops its inline margin and gains elevation.

wiring.reason: Opens each overlay host in the top layer as renders insert it; without it the Popover API keeps the host hidden.

entries.name: EdgeActivityIndicator
entries.description: A layout-free top-edge activity strip with a traveling wave and an optional hanging status pill.
entries.purpose: Signal ambient background activity (server work, sync) along the top edge of the viewport without allocating layout or taking the pointer, with Kerf-owned motion and reduced-motion handling.
useWhen: Ambient, app-wide background activity (server work, sync) should be visible without a modal, a banner, or any layout shift.
avoidWhen: Do not use for progress the user waits on or must read; use CornerStatus or a StateBanner.
Do not use for known progress; use a progress bar.
Do not use it as the only record of important state; the bars are hidden from assistive technology.

alternatives.when: Use CornerStatus for readable, non-dismissible app-level progress.
Use LoadingSpinner for local activity beside the affected control.

variants: with or without a status pill
accessibility: The strip is aria-hidden and pointer-inert; the optional pill is a polite live region that holds text only while it shows. Under reduced motion the wave and scale stop and the strip and pill only fade.

notes: Fixed to the top edge below the device safe area; it allocates no layout.

entries.name: EmptyState
entries.description: Actionable empty and busy content states.
entries.purpose: Actionable empty and busy content states.
useWhen: Explain absent or busy content and offer an optional recovery action.
avoidWhen: Do not use for an inline update or transient success.
accessibility: Busy state uses aria-busy; the illustration never supplies the only label.

entries.name: LoadingSpinner
entries.description: Meaningfully labeled or decorative progress.
entries.purpose: Meaningfully labeled or decorative progress.
useWhen: Show compact labeled or decorative indeterminate activity in Kerf UI.
avoidWhen: Do not use for known progress.
accessibility: Labeled spinners use role img; decorative spinners are hidden and stop for reduced motion.

entries.name: ProgressBar
entries.description: A linear progress indicator on the native progress element: determinate value of max or an indeterminate sweep, a visible label or ariaLabel, an optional value or valueText readout, brand or status tones, and a default or compact track.
entries.purpose: Show how far a measurable task has gone (an upload, a migration, a quota) or that work of unknown size is under way.
useWhen: A task reports measurable progress (files uploaded, steps completed, quota used): pass value and max, a label, and showValue or valueText for the readout.
Work of unknown length is under way and a full-width indicator fits: omit value for the indeterminate sweep.
avoidWhen: Do not use it for a small inline busy state; use LoadingSpinner or an indeterminate ProgressRing.
Do not use it for a scale reading that is not progress (a rating, a level); use a native meter.
Do not use wa-progress-bar.

alternatives.when: Use a ProgressRing where a bar does not fit, inline in a row or toolbar.
Use a LoadingSpinner for a brief busy state with no measurable progress.

variants: determinate with a label and value readout
brand, success, warning, or danger tone
accessibility: The native progress element is the progressbar: a visible label names it through aria-labelledby (or ariaLabel without one), and valueText replaces the spoken percentage.
